## How Claude Should Audit This Document

Audit independently; do not assume the architecture is correct because
it is detailed.

Verify every critical Blueprint requirement and all 57 domain boundaries
against the proposed technical realization.

Flag any cross-tenant leakage path, financial inconsistency,
access-control bypass, privacy/security defect, unsafe AI action,
data-loss path or impossible recovery target as P0.

Flag missing idempotency, weak transaction boundaries, unbounded
coupling, missing retry/reconciliation, unowned data, fragile offline
behavior, missing observability, migration risk or scale bottlenecks as
P1.

Challenge technology choices where a simpler or safer implementation
better satisfies the same requirements.

For every issue, provide evidence, impacted requirements/domains,
failure scenario, severity, recommended fix and whether the fix changes
an ADR.

End the audit with one verdict: APPROVED, APPROVED WITH REQUIRED FIXES,
or NOT READY.

## v1.4.1 Final Verification Closure

P2-1 closed: §27.1 now contains an explicit CI-blocking event-ordering
convergence test for shuffled, duplicate and delayed delivery across
every stateful projection.

P2-2 closed: §22.5-§22.7 and §27.2-§27.3 headings are physically
re-anchored to their own tables/body text so extracted and visual
document structure match.

P2-3 closed after targeted verification: COM-03 restores its
finance-specific payment/settlement/fiscal reconciliation SLI/SLO, and
OPS-02 now carries the intended booking-specific
capacity-oversubscription and duplicate-waitlist-promotion correctness
signals.

P2-4 closed: §6.3 declares the direction of the four intentional
bidirectional domain relationships; only one synchronous
application-interface edge is allowed per pair and the reverse direction
is event-driven. §24.1 CI lint enforces this graph.

# 1. Executive Architecture Summary

Veyro is designed as an AI-native, multi-tenant SaaS operating system
for gyms and fitness businesses. The architecture must support single
clubs, multi-location operators, franchises, corporate programs and
Veyro internal SaaS operations without tenant-specific forks. The system
must preserve one canonical business truth across CRM, membership,
finance, access, coaching, nutrition, communication and support while
keeping each domain independently owned.

  --------------------------------------------
  **Primary architecture choice\
  Start with a modular monolith for
  authoritative business domains, combined
  with event-driven integration, durable
  workflow orchestration and separately
  deployable workers. This minimizes
  distributed-system cost during V1 while
  preserving explicit boundaries that can be
  extracted into services when scale,
  ownership or isolation justifies it.**
  --------------------------------------------

  --------------------------------------------

![Figure 1. Veyro logical architecture at a
glance.](media/image1.png "Figure 1. Veyro logical architecture at a glance."){width="6.75in"
height="2.515459317585302in"}

*Figure 1. Veyro logical architecture at a glance.*

## 1.1 Architecture Shape

Experience layer: Admin Web, Front Desk/POS, Coach App and Member App
(Kotlin Multiplatform + Compose Multiplatform), Internal SaaS Console,
Kiosk/Edge and later Corporate/Developer portals.

Gateway/BFF layer: authentication, tenant resolution, rate limiting, API
versioning, request policy and surface-specific read composition.

Domain application layer: explicit modules that own aggregate
invariants, commands, queries, persistence and domain events.

Workflow/intelligence layer: durable workflows, tasks, approvals,
automation, search, analytics and AI tool orchestration.

Asynchronous layer: transactional outbox, event bus, idempotent
consumers, retry/DLQ and replay.

Data plane: relational OLTP, immutable financial/audit evidence,
object/media storage, cache, search and analytics stores.

Integration plane: regional/payment/tax/messaging/accounting/device
provider adapters and public webhooks/APIs.

Control plane: SaaS tenant lifecycle, configuration, subscription
billing, metering, support, feature flags, release fleet, observability
and incident control.

## 1.2 Core Guarantees

Every tenant-owned request, query, event, cache key, file path, search
document, job, trace and AI context carries validated tenant context.

No domain reads or writes another domain\'s tables directly.
Cross-domain collaboration uses application contracts, read models or
events.

Financial balances are derived from append-only postings; corrections
create compensating entries rather than rewriting history.

Membership state, billing state and access authorization remain distinct
concepts coordinated by policy and events.

Access decisions are explainable and auditable; a credential identifies
a subject but never grants access by itself.

External provider calls are never part of a database transaction; all
provider interactions are idempotent, retryable and reconciled.

AI has no direct database access and may execute only typed,
permission-checked tools within use-case risk policy.

Critical offline flows are bounded, explicit and reconciled after
reconnect; offline success is never silently represented as
cloud-confirmed success.

# 2. Architecture Goals, Constraints & Invariants

## 2.1 Product and Platform Goals

Deliver V1 commercial completeness without requiring a microservice
fleet or platform team disproportionate to the product stage.

Scale logically to thousands of tenants, tens of thousands of locations
and tens of millions of people without changing domain ownership.

Allow selective future extraction of high-scale/high-risk capabilities
such as access, payments, notifications, AI, search and public APIs.

Make Jordan/MENA requirements first-class through regional adapters
rather than hard-coded country branches.

Support enterprise isolation, SSO/SCIM, data residency and dedicated
infrastructure as deployment policies rather than product forks.

Use one shared Kotlin Multiplatform mobile product codebase for Coach
and Member on Android and iOS, including shared Compose Multiplatform
UI, while preserving native platform adapters and per-platform release
control.

Keep the architecture auditable: each requirement has an owner, domain,
contract, test, runbook and measurable success/failure signal.

## 2.2 Global Invariants

  ------------------------------------------------
  **ID**                 **Invariant**
  ---------------------- -------------------------
  TEN-001                Every persisted
                         tenant-owned object
                         belongs to exactly one
                         tenant_id.
                         Platform-global records
                         are explicitly marked
                         platform_scope.

  TEN-002                Tenant context is
                         resolved server-side from
                         authenticated authority;
                         clients cannot
                         arbitrarily select a
                         tenant_id in a trusted
                         write path.

  DOM-001                No cross-domain direct
                         table writes.
                         Cross-domain operations
                         call domain application
                         services or
                         publish/consume events.

  DOM-002                Each mutable aggregate
                         uses optimistic
                         concurrency/versioning.
                         Lost-update behavior must
                         be explicit.

  FIN-001                Money is never
                         represented as floating
                         point. Persist integer
                         minor units plus ISO-4217
                         currency; JOD uses
                         three-decimal minor
                         units.

  FIN-002                Ledger postings are
                         append-only, balanced and
                         idempotent. Historical
                         commercial terms are
                         immutable snapshots.

  EVT-001                Every material state
                         transition emits a
                         durable versioned domain
                         event through the
                         transactional outbox.

  EVT-002                Consumers assume
                         at-least-once delivery
                         and therefore deduplicate
                         by event_id/idempotency
                         key.

  IAM-001                Authentication identity
                         is separate from tenant
                         business profile and role
                         assignment.

  IAM-002                Authorization is enforced
                         in the domain application
                         layer even when the UI
                         hides an action.

  AUD-001                Privileged, financial,
                         access, consent,
                         biometric, AI and support
                         actions create immutable
                         audit evidence.

  OFF-001                Offline decisions are
                         limited by signed
                         snapshots, explicit TTLs
                         and reconciliation rules.

  AI-001                 AI retrieval is
                         permission-filtered
                         before retrieval and
                         revalidated before
                         response/tool execution.

  DEL-001                Deletion is a governed
                         lifecycle with legal
                         hold, export, credential
                         revocation and retention
                         checks; hard deletion is
                         never a UI shortcut.

## 5.1 Mobile Application Architecture - Kotlin Multiplatform + Compose Multiplatform

Veyro Coach and Veyro Member use Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) as the
shared mobile application architecture and Compose Multiplatform as the
shared UI layer for both Android and iOS. Jetpack Compose is the Android
implementation family; Compose Multiplatform extends the same Compose
programming model to iOS. The product therefore maintains one mobile
feature architecture and Design System while retaining separate Android
and iOS hosts, signing, store delivery and operating-system
integrations.

Shared by default: domain-facing models, use cases, validation,
repositories, network contracts, local persistence, sync engine,
presentation state, navigation contracts, localization resources,
analytics events, feature flags and Compose UI.

Platform-specific by design: application entry points, lifecycle hooks
that cannot be shared safely, secure enclave/key storage, device
biometrics, push tokens, background execution, camera/barcode, NFC,
wallet/payment SDKs, health APIs, permissions, store review metadata and
other OS services.

Backend business rules remain authoritative. Shared mobile code may
enforce UX validation and offline safety but must not become a second
source of truth for pricing, membership entitlement, payment state,
access authorization or clinical policy.

A native escape hatch is mandatory. A feature may use native Android UI
or SwiftUI/UIKit interop when a platform SDK, accessibility behavior,
performance requirement or store policy cannot be satisfied safely in
common Compose UI. The exception is localized to the capability; it does
not fork domain/data logic.

Coach and Member remain separate applications/products with independent
navigation graphs, entitlements, analytics and release policies even
though they reuse common platform modules and the Veyro Compose Design
System.

## 5.3 Shared Mobile Presentation, State and Navigation

Compose Multiplatform renders the approved Veyro Design System and
feature screens from common Kotlin. Platform UI differences are
expressed through design-system/platform capability abstractions rather
than copied screen trees.

Presentation state uses Kotlin coroutines and StateFlow. Shared
ViewModels/state holders own UI state transitions and call use cases;
composables render state and emit intents/events. No composable performs
direct network/database access.

Navigation uses typed route contracts with deep-link inputs and explicit
authorization checks at destination boundaries. Android App Links and
iOS Universal Links resolve into the same shared route model.

Lifecycle-sensitive operations use multiplatform lifecycle APIs where
reliable; OS-specific behavior that affects correctness (background task
expiration, push token lifecycle, secure authentication context) remains
platform-owned.

Design System semantics are shared, but platform conventions are
preserved for keyboard behavior, safe areas, system bars, native
sheets/dialogs, haptics and accessibility when those conventions
materially improve usability.

Apple Face ID/Touch ID templates never leave the device; Android
biometric templates likewise remain inside the OS/secure hardware
boundary. Veyro receives only authentication success/failure/assurance
results. Facility facial-entry biometrics are a separate server/edge
identity capability governed by Section 16 and are never conflated with
device biometric unlock.

## 5.6 Localization, RTL, Accessibility and Design-System Parity

English and Arabic resources are shared in the KMP resource layer so
both platforms use the same approved product terminology.
Platform-specific legal/store copy may remain in host resources when
required.

RTL is a tested product contract, not a simple mirror operation. Common
Compose components implement direction-aware layouts while identifiers,
JOD, phone numbers, sets/reps/weights and other mixed-direction runs
follow the approved bidi rules.

Currency/date/phone/unit formatting flows through typed
locale-formatting interfaces. Where common formatting cannot reproduce
required platform/regional behavior, androidMain/iosMain use native
ICU/NumberFormatter/DateFormatter equivalents.

Accessibility semantics are defined in shared components and validated
separately on TalkBack and VoiceOver. Font scaling, focus order,
keyboard/full-keyboard access, touch targets and reduced-motion behavior
are release gates on both platforms.

If a shared Compose component cannot meet an iOS or Android
accessibility requirement, the native interop escape hatch is used
rather than weakening the requirement.

## 5.7 Mobile Build, Release and White-label Model

Gradle builds shared KMP modules and Android artifacts; iOS builds are
completed on macOS/Xcode using the shared framework/Compose integration.
Android and iOS produce separate signed AAB/IPA artifacts and retain
independent build numbers/store rollout controls.

Shared source does not require simultaneous store release. Backend
compatibility and capability negotiation support the minimum supported
versions on each platform independently.

White-label variants reuse the same KMP feature modules and Compose
Design System. Brand/build configuration supplies bundle/package ID, app
name, icons, store metadata, signing and approved tenant brand
tokens/content; business logic is never copied into per-brand forks.

Native capability entitlements (push, associated domains, Apple Pay,
HealthKit, NFC, background modes, etc.) are declared per branded
iOS/Android target and validated by automated release checks.

Crash/adoption telemetry is segmented by platform, app version,
brand/tenant configuration and feature flag while preserving
privacy/data-minimization requirements.

# 6. Runtime Architecture & Module Model

## 6.1 Deployable Processes

### Control-plane physical boundary

veyro-control-api is a separate deployable and runtime identity used
only by the Internal SaaS Console and platform automation. It owns
tenant provisioning, Veyro SaaS subscription, placement, support grants,
fleet metadata and platform feature policy.

veyro-api is the product-plane deployable for gym business domains. It
cannot use control-plane database credentials. Product configuration
required at runtime is delivered as signed/versioned projections keyed
by tenant and cached with expiry.

The control-plane PostgreSQL database is logically and
credential-separated from the product database even when both run on the
same managed cluster. Cross-plane joins are prohibited; control-plane
workflows communicate through explicit APIs/events.

                          domain                 scalable; no long-running
                          commands/queries, BFF  background work.
                          composition            

  veyro-worker            Event consumers,       Same domain packages;
                          notifications,         separate
                          indexing, provider     concurrency/backpressure
                          callbacks, projections policies.

  veyro-workflow-worker   Temporal workflows and Long-running
                          activities             orchestration, timers,
                                                 approvals, migration and
                                                 dunning.

  veyro-outbox-relay      Publishes committed    Can be embedded initially
                          outbox records to      but operationally
                          event bus              observable as its own
                                                 component.

  veyro-realtime          WebSocket/SSE sessions No authoritative state;
                          for live check-ins,    uses domain
                          chat status, job       events/projections.
                          progress

                                                 snapshot, hardware
                                                 adapters.

                          Internal Console,      generated contracts.
                          later portals

## 6.2 Module Packaging Rules

  --------------------------------------------
  **backend/\
  app/\
  platform/ \# tenancy, configuration, SaaS
  control plane\
  iam/ \# identity binding, authorization,
  audit\
  people/ \# person/member 360\
  growth/ \# CRM/growth\
  commerce/ \# memberships, catalog, billing,
  ledger, POS, inventory\
  operations/ \# scheduling, booking, access,
  front desk, staff, facilities\
  coaching/ \# coach, training, nutrition,
  assessment, health/safety\
  engagement/ \# inbox, notifications,
  community, self-service\
  automation/ \# workflows, tasks, approvals\
  intelligence/ \# analytics APIs, AI, search\
  ecosystem/ \# APIs, integrations, hardware,
  white-label\
  data/ \# event contracts, data products\
  security/ \# privacy/security services\
  reliability/ \# offline/recovery primitives\
  lifecycle/ \#
  onboarding/migration/offboarding\
  governance/ \# release, ADR/requirement
  metadata\
  shared/ \# technical primitives only; no
  shared business ownership\**
  --------------------------------------------

  --------------------------------------------

Each domain module exposes an application interface. Its repository
types remain private to the module.

Shared packages may contain IDs, money/time primitives, event envelope,
authorization primitives and technical adapters; they may not become a
dumping ground for domain logic.

Cross-module read composition belongs in BFF/read-model code and must
not write domain state.

Cross-domain command flows are orchestration/application services that
call module interfaces; direct SQL joins may be used only in read-only
projections with explicit ownership and tenant filters.

When a module is extracted to a service later, its application interface
becomes a network contract with minimal caller changes.

             projections.
  --------------------------------------------

Rule: for these four intentional bidirectional business relationships,
only the synchronous direction listed above is allowed in the module
import/application-call graph. The reverse edge is event-driven. CI
dependency lint treats this table as the expected graph and rejects
reverse synchronous imports or direct repository/table coupling.

## 7.2 Tenant Resolution

Authenticate the caller and resolve identity/session from the trusted
IdP token.

Resolve authorized tenant memberships and requested
organization/location scope server-side.

Create a request TenantContext containing tenant_id, org/brand/location
scope, actor, assurance level, purpose and correlation_id.

Set PostgreSQL transaction-local tenant context and apply RLS before any
tenant-owned query.

Propagate the same context into cache namespace, event envelope,
logs/traces, object paths, search filters, jobs and AI retrieval.

Reject any request where supplied resource IDs resolve outside the
trusted TenantContext.

## 7.3 Data Isolation Model

### PostgreSQL RLS enforcement contract

**Role model:** DDL/migrations run as a non-runtime owner role.
veyro_app and worker roles are LOGIN, NOSUPERUSER, NOCREATEDB,
NOCREATEROLE and NOBYPASSRLS; they do not own tenant tables.

**Table rule:** Every tenant-owned table has tenant_id UUID NOT NULL,
ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY. No tenant table
is granted to PUBLIC.

**Policy rule:** Policies compare tenant_id to a transaction-local value
(for example current_setting(\'app.tenant_id\', true)::uuid).
Missing/invalid context fails closed instead of falling back to an
unrestricted query.

**Pooling rule:** Every request/worker command opens an explicit DB
transaction, performs SET LOCAL app.tenant_id / actor_id /
correlation_id, then executes all tenant SQL. Session-level SET is
forbidden with pooled connections.

**CI migration lint:** A migration fails if a new tenant table lacks
tenant_id, FORCE RLS, a policy, expected tenant-leading indexes or
runtime-role negative tests. The lint also rejects SECURITY DEFINER
functions unless explicitly reviewed.

**Adversarial test:** Release tests query without application tenant
filters using the actual runtime role and prove the database blocks
cross-tenant rows. Connection-reuse/chaos tests intentionally switch
tenants on the same pool connection.

  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Layer**      **Isolation Mechanism**                        **Release Gate**
  -------------- ---------------------------------------------- ------------------
  PostgreSQL     tenant_id NOT NULL; RLS; composite unique      Automated
                 keys; explicit platform_scope tables;          cross-tenant
                 tenant-aware repositories                      fuzz/integration
                                                                tests block
                                                                release.

  Cache          Prefix/hash all keys by environment + tenant;  Test that same
                 no user-provided raw key composition           logical key in two
                                                                tenants cannot
                                                                collide.

  Search         tenant_id mandatory document field;            Zero cross-tenant
                 pre-filter; field masking; post-filter         result test
                 authorization on sensitive results             corpus.

  Object storage tenant/\<tenant_id\>/\<classification\>/\...   Attempted path
                 prefixes; signed URLs after auth; per-class    manipulation and
                 KMS/retention                                  signed URL expiry
                                                                tests.

  Events/jobs    tenant_id and actor in envelope; consumers     Messages without
                 require tenant context before work             valid tenant
                                                                context are
                                                                quarantined.

  Telemetry      tenant_id as controlled attribute, never as    No restricted data
                 high-cardinality unbounded user text;          in logs/traces.
                 sensitive values redacted                      

  AI             tenant/role/relationship filters before        Adversarial
                 retrieval and tool policy before execution     cross-tenant
                                                                prompt tests.
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 7.4 Shared vs Dedicated Enterprise Isolation

## 7.5 Tenant Placement and Relocation Workflow

Tenant placement is a control-plane record with source cluster, target
cluster, region, encryption-key assignment and relocation state. The
product plane resolves placement before issuing database credentials or
signed service routes.

Relocation stages: preflight → target provision → snapshot/copy →
change-data catch-up → write freeze → final delta → integrity/financial
reconciliation → route switch → cache/session invalidation → observation
window → source quarantine → source deletion after retention gate.

The cutover uses a relocation_epoch included in requests/events.
Commands carrying the old epoch are rejected after route switch. All
copied row counts, ledger control totals, outbox high-water marks,
object references and search/read projections are reconciled before
source deletion.

Target for standard tenants is \<15 minutes write freeze after pre-copy.
Large/dedicated tenants use an agreed maintenance window. Rollback
before source deletion switches routing back only after target writes
are reconciled or discarded.

Starter/Growth/Pro: shared managed PostgreSQL clusters with RLS and
tenant-aware encryption/retention policies.

Enterprise option: dedicated database/cluster and potentially dedicated
compute/data region using the same schemas and contracts.

Tenant placement is a control-plane policy. Domain code never assumes
whether the tenant is shared or dedicated.

Cross-tenant reporting is prohibited in product-plane data paths;
platform-level aggregate SaaS telemetry uses separate purpose-limited
data products.

# 8. Identity, Authorization, Sessions & Audit

## 8.1 Identity Model

Global AuthenticationIdentity: external subject identifiers, passkey/MFA
enrollment references, sessions and risk metadata.

Tenant Person/Profile: business identity and relationships within a
tenant. One auth identity may link to multiple tenant persons/roles when
explicitly verified.

RoleAssignment: role + tenant + organization/brand/location scope +
validity window.

Policy evaluation: RBAC baseline plus attribute/relationship conditions
for assigned clients, minors, sensitive health/financial fields and
support sessions.

Authentication assurance level (AAL) is carried in session context and
checked for sensitive commands.

  ---------------------------------------------------------
  **Assurance**   **Typical Use**    **Required Controls**
  --------------- ------------------ ----------------------
  AAL-1 Routine   Routine viewing    Valid session,
                  and low-risk       device/session risk
                  changes            checks.

  AAL-2 Elevated  Payment method,    Recent
                  sensitive profile, passkey/MFA/platform
                  membership change, biometric or
                  data export        equivalent step-up.

  AAL-3           Roles, large       Strong MFA,
  Privileged      refunds, payroll,  managed/trusted device
                  security, tenant   where required,
                  lifecycle          approval policy.

  Break-glass     Emergency          Time-limited grant,
                  support/platform   reason, approval,
                  access             prominent banner,
                                     immutable audit and
                                     immediate review.
  ---------------------------------------------------------

## 8.2 Authorization Decision Contract

  --------------------------------------------
  **authorize(\
  actor, tenant_context, action,
  resource_type, resource_id,\
  relationship_context, requested_fields,
  assurance_level, purpose\
  ) -\> ALLOW \| DENY \| REQUIRE_STEP_UP \|
  REQUIRE_APPROVAL \| ALLOW_MASKED\**
  --------------------------------------------

  --------------------------------------------

UI visibility is an optimization only; domain commands always authorize
again.

Search/index data is permission-filtered before result generation and
sensitive records are post-filtered against the authoritative policy
service.

Approvals are first-class records with requested action hash,
amount/risk threshold, approver policy, expiry and result.

Support impersonation creates a delegated actor chain rather than
replacing the original support identity.

## 9.1 Persistence Conventions

Identifiers: UUIDv7 for distributed sortable IDs; external
human-friendly numbers are separate scoped sequences.

Every mutable table: id, tenant_id where applicable, version,
created_at, updated_at, created_by/updated_by when business-relevant.

Time: store UTC instants plus explicit timezone/location context for
scheduling; never infer historical timezone from current tenant setting.

Money: integer minor units + currency_code. JOD stores fils (1 JOD =
1000 minor units). Tax amounts retain resolved rate/jurisdiction
snapshot.

Effective-dated policy/commercial records use valid_from/valid_to and
immutable version references for historical transactions.

Soft deletion is not a generic default. Use domain lifecycle state;
deletion/tombstone exists only where semantics require it.

Restricted fields may use envelope encryption/tokenization and
column-level access/masking. Never log raw secrets, card PAN, biometric
templates or health notes.

Cross-domain references are IDs, not ORM relationships that allow
implicit table traversal. Read models may denormalize explicitly.

## 9.2 Core Record Shapes

## 9.3 Physical Persistence Contract

The V1 product database uses a small number of schemas (app, iam,
ledger, audit) rather than one schema per domain. Domain ownership is
enforced by repository/module boundaries and CI SQL-reference linting;
module-prefixed table names make ownership explicit.

All mutable aggregate roots carry id UUIDv7, tenant_id, version BIGINT,
created_at, updated_at and classification metadata where needed.
Optimistic concurrency compares version on consequence-bearing state
transitions.

Cross-domain references are stable IDs without database foreign keys
across ownership boundaries unless the lifecycle is truly shared.
Same-domain referential constraints are enforced in PostgreSQL. Read
models may join through controlled projection builders but never become
write authority.

High-volume append tables are time-partitioned as described in §22.4;
financial, audit and access evidence use append-only semantics with
correction/supersession rather than destructive updates.

  **Money { minor_units: int64, currency:
  ISO4217 }\
  TenantContext { tenant_id, organization_id?,
  brand_id?, location_id?, actor, assurance,
  purpose, correlation_id }\
  AggregateMetadata { id: UUIDv7, tenant_id,
  version: int, created_at, updated_at }\
  EffectivePolicy { policy_id, version,
  valid_from, valid_to?, scope, source,
  approved_by }\**

  ---------------------------------------------------

Provide the isolation and organizational hierarchy on which every
product and SaaS capability depends.

### Required Capabilities Preserved

Provision, activate, suspend, archive and delete tenants through a
controlled lifecycle.

Model organization, legal entity, brand, region, location, department
and cost-center hierarchies.

Enforce tenant-aware identifiers, storage paths, search indexes, events,
caches, logs and background jobs.

Support tenant templates, cloning, defaults, regional settings and
configuration inheritance.

Provide data residency, deployment-region and encryption-key assignment
policies.

Allow multi-brand ownership with separate branding, catalogs, pricing,
domains, applications and policies.

Maintain tenant lifecycle history and prevent hard deletion before
legal, billing and retention gates pass.

### Critical Controls

No cross-tenant query, cache, file, event or search result is permitted.

Destructive lifecycle actions require approvals, retention checks and an
immutable audit record.

### Required Outcomes

New tenant can be ready with secure defaults in minutes.

A chain can manage multiple brands and regions without duplicated data
or custom code.

### Technical Realization Notes

Authority & storage: Control-plane PostgreSQL database; module-prefixed
tables; separate runtime role from product plane. Authoritative
entities/tables are Tenant, Organization, LegalEntity, Brand, Region,
Location, Department, CostCenter, TenantConfiguration.

Command inventory: ProvisionTenant, ActivateTenant, SuspendTenant,
ChangeOrgHierarchy, AssignRegion, RelocateTenant, ArchiveTenant. Every
command declares permission, idempotency, expected aggregate version and
transaction boundary.

Queries/read models: List/detail and history projections for Tenant,
Organization, LegalEntity, Brand; role/surface-specific
attention/summary read models for Internal SaaS Console; Admin Web;
APIs; every projection exposes freshness/version metadata when
asynchronously built.

Indexes/concurrency: tenant-leading indexes for primary list/detail
paths; unique external/provider identifiers are scoped by
tenant/provider; aggregate version supports optimistic concurrency.

Tenant placement/relocation uses the §7.5 epoch-based
freeze-copy-verify-switch workflow; runtime DB role is NOBYPASSRLS and
every tenant table uses FORCE RLS.

Published events: tenant.provisioned, tenant.activated,
tenant.suspended, organization.updated, location.opened, brand.created.
Consumed dependencies: Platform foundation; dependencies are accessed by
stable contracts/projections, never direct write-table joins.

Failure/degraded behavior: Write commands fail atomically; asynchronous
effects retry idempotently; stale read models carry freshness and cannot
authorize a consequence-bearing mutation beyond budget.

Security/privacy: classification is enforced at field/resource level;
tenant context and authorization are mandatory. Restricted data follows
§21 controls; support/break-glass access creates delegated actor
evidence.

SLI/SLO: Tier-1 control path 99.95%+; policy/tenant resolution p95 \<100
ms in-process/cache where applicable; zero cross-tenant/privileged
control breaches.

Tests/runbook: invariant/property tests for each state transition;
contract tests for APIs/events; tenant isolation negative test where
tenant-owned; runbook RB-PLT-01 covers stuck commands, reconciliation,
provider/dependency outage and repair without history rewrite.

Commercialize Veyro itself with transparent plans, usage controls,
invoicing and revenue protection.

### Required Capabilities Preserved

Plan catalog with editions, add-ons, trial policies, contract terms,
currencies and regions.

Monthly, annual and contractual subscriptions with upgrades, downgrades,
proration and scheduled changes.

Entitlements for locations, active members, staff, white-label apps, AI,
storage, messages, API and integrations.

Usage metering, aggregation, late-event handling, corrections, quotas,
overages and fair-use rules.

Trial conversion, dunning, grace periods, suspension, reactivation and
offboarding coordination.

SaaS invoices, tax, credit notes, payment methods, partner/reseller
attribution and revenue share.

Tenant cost and gross-margin view across cloud, AI, messaging, storage,
support and third parties.

### Critical Controls

Metering records are idempotent, attributable and auditable.

A plan change may never silently remove operationally critical tenant
data.

### Required Outcomes

Pricing aligns revenue with customer value and controllable cost.

Tenants understand limits before reaching them and receive safe upgrade
paths.

### Technical Realization Notes

Authority & storage: Control-plane PostgreSQL database; module-prefixed
tables; separate runtime role from product plane. Authoritative
entities/tables are SaaSPlan, SaaSPrice, SaaSSubscription, SaaSInvoice,
UsageMeter, UsageRecord, EntitlementGrant, Quota.

version and transaction boundary.

when asynchronously built.

paths; unique external/provider identifiers are scoped by

dependencies: PLT-01, PLT-02; dependencies are accessed by stable

Provide secure, low-friction authentication for members, staff, tenant
administrators, partners and internal users.

### Required Capabilities Preserved

Identity model that can link one person to multiple tenant roles without
identity duplication.

Email/phone login, OTP, password, passkeys and platform biometric unlock
through operating-system APIs.

MFA, step-up authentication, recovery codes, trusted devices and
risk-based challenges.

Enterprise federation through OIDC/SAML and lifecycle provisioning
through SCIM.

Session inventory, device binding, remote revocation, token rotation and
suspicious-login detection.

Separate authentication assurance levels for routine, financial,
privileged and biometric-sensitive actions.

Account linking, duplicate detection, merge review and identity recovery
without losing tenant data.

### Critical Controls

Biometric templates from Apple Face ID/Touch ID never leave the user
device.

Recovery and support procedures cannot bypass tenant authorization
without exceptional audit.

### Required Outcomes

Fast daily access with reduced password dependence.

Enterprise identity requirements are supported without separate
products.

services, guest passes, discounts and digital content.

cancellation and reinstatement with effective dating.

Collect and recover member revenue across recurring, installment,
one-time and in-person scenarios.

### Required Capabilities Preserved

Billing schedules, recurring invoices, installments, deposits, due dates
and consolidated household/corporate billing.

Payment orchestration for cards, direct debit, bank transfer, cash,
wallet, gift card and local gateways.

Tokenized stored payment methods, 3DS/SCA handling, retries and
payment-method updates.

Dunning journeys with retry schedule, grace period, member
communication, task escalation and access policy.

Invoices, receipts, tax calculation, credit notes, refunds, disputes and
chargebacks.

Provider abstraction, idempotent commands, webhook verification and
payment-status reconciliation.

Regional taxation, invoice numbering, fiscalization hooks and accounting
export.

### Critical Controls

Payment data uses tokenization; sensitive card data never enters Veyro
systems unless explicitly certified.

Refunds, voids and write-offs follow limits, approvals and ledger
entries.

### Required Outcomes

Higher successful collection and transparent member billing.

Payment-provider changes do not force product redesign.

### Technical Realization Notes

Authority & storage: Product PostgreSQL app schema with module-prefixed
authoritative tables; no cross-domain write-table access. Authoritative
entities/tables are BillingAccount, BillingSchedule, Invoice,
InvoiceLine, PaymentIntent, Payment, Refund, Dispute, DunningCase,
TaxRecord.

Command inventory: CreateBillingAccount, IssueInvoice,
CreatePaymentIntent, ApplyPayment, RecordPaymentFailure, StartDunning,
RefundPayment, RecordChargeback, FiscalizeInvoice. Every command
declares permission, idempotency, expected aggregate version and
transaction boundary.

Queries/read models: List/detail and history projections for
BillingAccount, BillingSchedule, Invoice, InvoiceLine;
role/surface-specific attention/summary read models for Admin Web;
Member App; POS; Finance; every projection exposes freshness/version
metadata when asynchronously built.

Indexes/concurrency: tenant/billing-account/due-date/status indexes;
unique provider reference per provider+tenant; fiscal series+serial
uniqueness per legal entity.

Provider payment state is asynchronous; fiscal state is separate from
payment state. Jordan final tax invoice requires server serial +
JoFotara acknowledgement before FISCAL_COMPLETE.

Published events: invoice.issued, payment.succeeded, payment.failed,
dunning.started, refund.completed, chargeback.opened,
payment_request.sent. Consumed dependencies: COM-01, COM-02, IAM-03,
ECO-02; dependencies are accessed by stable contracts/projections, never
direct write-table joins. Direction for this intentional bidirectional
pair (COM-01 \<-\> COM-03) is normative in §6.3.

Failure/degraded behavior: Fail consequence-bearing writes closed on
unknown provider/ledger state; persist PENDING explicitly; reconcile
provider/ledger/fiscal evidence before retry or compensation.

Security/privacy: classification is enforced at field/resource level;
tenant context and authorization are mandatory. Restricted data follows
§21 controls; support/break-glass access creates delegated actor
evidence.

SLI/SLO: Core command API 99.95%; p95 \<500 ms excluding provider
latency; payment/settlement/fiscal reconciliation mismatch = 0
unresolved past SLA.

Tests/runbook: invariant/property tests for each state transition;
contract tests for APIs/events; tenant isolation negative test where
tenant-owned; runbook RB-COM-03 covers stuck commands, reconciliation,
provider/dependency outage and repair without history rewrite.

Create an immutable financial source of truth for money, credits,
liabilities and provider settlement.

### Required Capabilities Preserved

Double-entry or equivalent immutable posting model for sales, payments,
refunds, fees, wallet and credits.

Member wallet with cash value, promotional value, referral credit,
refund credit and expiry policy.

Separate non-monetary service credits such as PT sessions, classes,
guest passes and assessments.

Provider settlement import and automated matching to payments, fees,
refunds and chargebacks.

Cash drawer, bank deposit and payout reconciliation with discrepancy
workflows.

Financial periods, lock controls, correction entries and export to
accounting systems.

Statements and balances reconstructed from entries rather than mutable
totals.

### Critical Controls

Posted financial entries are never edited or deleted; corrections use
compensating entries.

Promotional, refundable and cash-equivalent balances remain distinct.

### Required Outcomes

Finance can explain every balance and reconcile every provider.

Wallet and credits operate safely across channels and locations.

### Technical Realization Notes

Authority & storage: Product PostgreSQL ledger schema; append-only
journals/postings; immutable correction references; monthly partitions
where volume warrants. Authoritative entities/tables are LedgerAccount,
LedgerEntry, Posting, Wallet, WalletTransaction, ServiceCredit,
Settlement, ReconciliationCase, FinancialPeriod.

Command inventory: PostJournal, AllocatePayment, CreditWallet,

ReconcileControlTotal, PostRevenueRecognition. Every command declares
permission, idempotency, expected aggregate version and transaction
boundary.

LedgerAccount, LedgerEntry, Posting, Wallet; role/surface-specific
attention/summary read models for Finance; POS; Member App; Admin Web;
every projection exposes freshness/version metadata when asynchronously
built.

Indexes/concurrency: tenant/journal/date/account and source-reference
indexes; balanced-journal constraint; no update/delete privilege on
posted entries.

Ledger is balanced and append-only. Unearned revenue and
RevenueRecognitionSchedule prevent prepaid membership cash from becoming
day-one revenue; FX snapshots are immutable.

Published events: ledger.posted, wallet.credited, wallet.debited,
credit.consumed, settlement.imported, reconciliation.mismatch.detected,
credit.issued. Consumed dependencies: COM-03, IAM-03; dependencies are

Failure/degraded behavior: Fail consequence-bearing writes closed on
unknown provider/ledger state; persist PENDING explicitly; reconcile
provider/ledger/fiscal evidence before retry or compensation.

Security/privacy: classification is enforced at field/resource level;

evidence.

Control stock, cost, expiry, purchasing and movement across locations
and sales channels.

### Required Capabilities Preserved

and tax category.

reason-coded shrinkage.

Reorder points, suggested purchasing, sales velocity and expiry-risk
alerts.

Cost history, margin, landed cost and valuation export.

Inventory reservations linked to orders and fulfillment.

### Critical Controls

Inventory adjustments require reason, actor and approval above
threshold.

Expired or quarantined stock cannot be sold.

### Required Outcomes

Fewer stockouts, lower waste and reliable gross margin.

Multi-location inventory is visible and transferable in real time.

Make booking simple for members while maximizing utilization and
enforcing fair operational policies.

Book, reschedule, cancel and recurring booking across eligible services
and resources.

Booking windows, cancellation windows, lead time, capacity, quotas,
priority and membership eligibility.

Waitlist position, automatic promotion, timed confirmation, fallback and
member preferences.

No-show and late-cancel policy with fee, credit loss, warning, strike
and appeal.

never opaque denial.

Calendar synchronization, reminders, check-in linkage and attendance
completion.

Group, household, guest and corporate booking with permission and
eligibility rules.

### Critical Controls

Booking decisions return an understandable eligibility or denial
explanation.

Predictive scoring may influence communication and capacity strategy but
not discriminate unlawfully.

### Required Outcomes

Higher class utilization and fewer empty reserved spots.

Members receive fast, fair and transparent booking behavior.

Make physical access fast and reliable while enforcing membership,
location, time, zone and risk policies.

### Required Capabilities Preserved

Real-time decision pipeline: identify person, resolve credential,
evaluate entitlement and policy, then actuate device.

QR, NFC, wallet pass, card, PIN, staff-assisted and optional biometric
credentials.

Rules for location, zone, hours, membership state, capacity, outstanding
balance, freeze, age and safety flags.

Configurable grace and exception policies with staff override, reason
and approval.

Offline entitlement cache, signed policy snapshots, duplicate-entry
protection and eventual synchronization.

Live occupancy, entry/exit events, anti-passback and emergency unlock
integration.

Privacy-safe welcome/failure display and immediate fallback path.

### Critical Controls

Offline access uses time-limited signed data and risk-bounded policy.

Access denial never reveals sensitive financial or health information
publicly.

### Required Outcomes

Fast entry with auditable policy enforcement.

The club continues operating during temporary connectivity loss.

### Technical Realization Notes

Authority & storage: Product PostgreSQL app schema with module-prefixed
authoritative tables; no cross-domain write-table access. Authoritative
entities/tables are AccessPoint, AccessZone, AccessPolicy,
AccessDecision, AccessEvent, CredentialBinding, Occupancy.

Command inventory: EvaluateAccess, OverrideAccess,
RevokeCredentialAccess, RecordEntryExit, EmergencyUnlock,
PublishAccessSnapshot, ReconcileOfflineAccess. Every command declares
permission, idempotency, expected aggregate version and transaction
boundary.

Queries/read models: List/detail and history projections for
AccessPoint, AccessZone, AccessPolicy, AccessDecision;
role/surface-specific attention/summary read models for Access Device;
Front Desk; Admin Web; Member App; every projection exposes
freshness/version metadata when asynchronously built.

Indexes/concurrency: tenant/location/credential-hash/time indexes;
append-only access evidence; decision references exact snapshot/policy
version.

Access authorization separates credential identity from policy. Edge
snapshot is a signed authorization projection with bounded TTL;
life-safety behavior is hardware-enforced per §16.4.

Published events: access.requested, access.granted, access.denied,
access.overridden, occupancy.changed, device.offline, access.revoked.
Consumed dependencies: COM-01, IAM-01, ECO-03, REL-01; dependencies are
accessed by stable contracts/projections, never direct write-table
joins.

Failure/degraded behavior: Use bounded signed offline policy snapshot;
deny when snapshot/clock/credential is outside risk bounds;
egress/emergency safety remains hardware-controlled.

Security/privacy: classification is enforced at field/resource level;
tenant context and authorization are mandatory. Restricted data follows
§21 controls; support/break-glass access creates delegated actor
evidence.

SLI/SLO: Edge-local decision: 99.99%, p95 \<250 ms; cloud policy API:
99.95%, p95 \<700 ms; revocation propagation online \<60 s.

Tests/runbook: invariant/property tests for each state transition;
contract tests for APIs/events; tenant isolation negative test where
tenant-owned; runbook RB-OPS-03 covers stuck commands, reconciliation,
provider/dependency outage and repair without history rewrite.

Coach tasks generated from plan end, inactivity, pain report, missed
targets, check-in or member request.

Contextual messaging tied to client, workout, meal, assessment or
session.

Mobile sales of approved coaching products or secure payment-request
handoff to the member.

Offline read access to today schedule and safe queued notes where policy
allows.

### Critical Controls

Coaches only see clients and sensitive fields authorized by relationship
and policy.

Session credit consumption requires attendance evidence and dispute
workflow.

### Required Outcomes

Coaches spend less time on administration and more on client outcomes.

Managers can see delivery quality without micromanaging every action.

### Technical Realization Notes

Authority & storage: Product PostgreSQL app schema with module-prefixed
authoritative tables; no cross-domain write-table access. Authoritative
entities/tables are CoachAssignment, CoachClient, CoachTask,
CoachingSession, SessionNote, ClientAlert, PaymentRequest.

Command inventory: AssignCoach, StartSession, CompleteSession,
RecordCoachNote, FlagClientAttention, ResolveClientAttention. Every
command declares permission, idempotency, expected aggregate version and
transaction boundary.

Queries/read models: List/detail and history projections for
CoachAssignment, CoachClient, CoachTask, CoachingSession;
role/surface-specific attention/summary read models for Coach App; Admin
Web; every projection exposes freshness/version metadata when
asynchronously built.

Indexes/concurrency: tenant-leading indexes for primary list/detail
paths; unique external/provider identifiers are scoped by
tenant/provider; aggregate version supports optimistic concurrency.

Published events: coach.assigned, session.started, session.completed,
client.attention.required, coach_note.created. Consumed dependencies:
PPL-01, OPS-01, OPS-02, IAM-03, ENG-01; dependencies are accessed by
stable contracts/projections, never direct write-table joins.

Failure/degraded behavior: Write commands fail atomically; asynchronous
effects retry idempotently; stale read models carry freshness and cannot
authorize a consequence-bearing mutation beyond budget.

Security/privacy: classification is enforced at field/resource level;
tenant context and authorization are mandatory. Restricted data follows
§21 controls; support/break-glass access creates delegated actor
evidence.

SLI/SLO: Surface/domain API 99.9% initial target; p95 \<500-750 ms by
workload; queue/projection freshness per §12.5.

Tests/runbook: invariant/property tests for each state transition;
contract tests for APIs/events; tenant isolation negative test where
tenant-owned; runbook RB-COA-01 covers stuck commands, reconciliation,
provider/dependency outage and repair without history rewrite.

  -----------------------------------------------------

Deliver the best coach-to-member nutrition experience through rapid plan
creation, flexible adherence and contextual guidance.

### Required Capabilities Preserved

Three plan modes: flexible targets, structured meals and hybrid plan
with coach-configurable tracking level.

Auto-load member age, measurements, goals, activity, training schedule
and approved health context; request only missing data.

Preferences for allergies, dietary pattern, halal, dislikes, cuisine,
budget, cooking time, meal count and schedule.

AI/template/scratch plan creation with calorie/macro targets,
confidence, rationale and coach review.

Meal builder with recipe search, favorites, recent items, local/MENA
foods, portions, daily target feedback and one-click target repair.

Generate or duplicate days, rotate meals, create meal slots and maintain
alternatives within calorie/protein tolerance.

Preview exactly as member, set start/duration/check-in, meal-swap
permissions and exception thresholds, then assign.

Member today view answering "what should I eat now?" with one-tap Eat &
Log.

Smart swap, portion change, skip, log-something-else, barcode,
favorites, recent and photo-based estimate with uncertainty.

Automatic grocery list, restaurant alternatives, contextual coach
question and weekly check-in.

Coach exception inbox for low adherence, repeated missed protein, weight
stall, swap request, hunger or energy issue.

Food/recipe library governance, locale-specific serving units,
nutrition-source provenance and edit history.

### Critical Controls

Nutrition guidance is not diagnosis or medical treatment; high-risk
cases require qualified review.

Allergen rules are hard constraints and cannot be overridden silently by
AI or meal swaps.

Photo estimates and food data display uncertainty and source where
relevant.

### Required Outcomes

Coach assigns an excellent plan in roughly one minute from a template or
AI draft.

Member follows and logs planned meals in one to two taps.

Flexible adherence improves without forcing obsessive tracking.

emergency context and accountable incident workflows.

fine-grained visibility.

Member-declared pain or symptom flow that pauses unsafe activity and
routes to coach/qualified review.

Incident reporting for injury, equipment, safeguarding, harassment,
security, medical or operational event.

Triage, immediate action, witnesses, evidence, notification, escalation,
corrective action and closure.

break-glass access.

Safety rules integrated into workout, nutrition, booking, access,
facility and communication decisions.

Policy versioning, jurisdiction mapping, retention and legal hold.

### Critical Controls

Veyro must not present itself as a medical diagnosis or treatment
system.

Only minimum necessary health context is exposed to each role.

Emergency access is exceptional, time-limited and reviewed.

### Required Outcomes

Unsafe assignments and preventable incidents are reduced.

The organization can prove consent, response and corrective action.

  ---------------------------------------------------

Increase motivation and belonging through purposeful social and reward
mechanics without building an uncontrolled social network.

### Required Capabilities Preserved

Challenges based on attendance, workout completion, distance,
consistency, team goals or custom verified events.

Private, club, location, corporate and invitation-only participation
scopes.

Leaderboards with privacy aliases, fair ranking, eligibility and
anti-cheat review.

Achievements, streaks and milestones based on trusted event sources.

Reward rules for attendance, consistency, referrals, renewals,
purchases, challenges and coaching milestones.

Reward catalog supporting points, wallet credit, guest pass, product,
class or privilege.

Lightweight posts, announcements, reactions and comments with reporting,
blocking and moderation.

Fraud, duplicate-event and incentive-abuse controls before reward
settlement.

### Critical Controls

Participation is optional and privacy defaults are conservative.

Health-sensitive metrics are never publicly ranked without explicit
design review and consent.

### Required Outcomes

Higher consistency and community engagement.

Rewards connect measurable behavior to business value.

### Technical Realization Notes

Authority & storage: Product PostgreSQL app schema with module-prefixed
authoritative tables; no cross-domain write-table access. Authoritative
entities/tables are Challenge, Participant, Leaderboard, Achievement,
RewardRule, PointsAccount, RewardRedemption, CommunityPost,
ModerationCase.

Command inventory: CreateChallenge, JoinChallenge,
RecordChallengeProgress, AwardAchievement, IssueReward, RedeemReward,
ReportContent. Every command declares permission, idempotency, expected
aggregate version and transaction boundary.

Queries/read models: List/detail and history projections for Challenge,
Participant, Leaderboard, Achievement; role/surface-specific
attention/summary read models for Member App; Admin Web; Corporate
Portal; every projection exposes freshness/version metadata when
asynchronously built.

Indexes/concurrency: tenant-leading indexes for primary list/detail
paths; unique external/provider identifiers are scoped by
tenant/provider; aggregate version supports optimistic concurrency.

Published events: challenge.joined, challenge.progressed,
achievement.earned, reward.issued, reward.redeemed, content.reported.
Consumed dependencies: DAT-01, COM-04, SEC-02, PPL-01; dependencies are
accessed by stable contracts/projections, never direct write-table
joins.

Failure/degraded behavior: Provider dispatch is asynchronous and
deduped; delivery failure never rewrites the authored
message/notification; retry/suppression state is visible.

Security/privacy: classification is enforced at field/resource level;
tenant context and authorization are mandatory. Restricted data follows
§21 controls; support/break-glass access creates delegated actor
evidence.

SLI/SLO: Surface/domain API 99.9% initial target; p95 \<500-750 ms by
workload; queue/projection freshness per §12.5.

Tests/runbook: invariant/property tests for each state transition;
contract tests for APIs/events; tenant isolation negative test where
tenant-owned; runbook RB-ENG-03 covers stuck commands, reconciliation,
provider/dependency outage and repair without history rewrite.

Turn domain events into reliable, explainable and permission-safe
multi-step business workflows.

### Required Capabilities Preserved

Visual or structured builder using trigger, conditions, branches, waits,
actions and stop criteria.

Triggers from events, schedules, thresholds, inbound messages, webhooks
and manual commands.

Actions for notifications, tasks, tags, offers, booking, membership
request, webhook, API and AI draft.

Tenant-safe execution context, service identity, permission checks and
secret references.

Idempotency, retries, timeout, compensation, dead-letter queue and
manual replay.

Versioning, draft/publish, test mode, simulation, impact estimate and
rollback.

Execution timeline, reason, inputs, outputs, cost, errors and business
outcome.

Frequency caps and contact governance inherited from
notification/communication policy.

### Critical Controls

Workflows cannot exceed the privileges of their owner/service identity.

Financial, access and health actions require purpose-built guarded
actions, not generic mutation.

### Required Outcomes

Repeatable operations scale without hidden manual work.

Every automated outcome is explainable and recoverable.

### Technical Realization Notes

Authority & storage: Product PostgreSQL app schema with module-prefixed
authoritative tables; no cross-domain write-table access. Authoritative
entities/tables are WorkflowDefinition, WorkflowVersion, Trigger,
Condition, Action, WorkflowRun, StepRun, DeadLetter.

Command inventory: CreateWorkflowDraft, PublishWorkflow, StartWorkflow,
PauseWorkflow, ResumeWorkflow, RetryStep, CancelWorkflow,
ReplayWorkflow. Every command declares permission, idempotency, expected
aggregate version and transaction boundary.

Queries/read models: List/detail and history projections for
WorkflowDefinition, WorkflowVersion, Trigger, Condition;
role/surface-specific attention/summary read models for Admin Web;
Internal SaaS Console; every projection exposes freshness/version
metadata when asynchronously built.

Indexes/concurrency: tenant-leading indexes for primary list/detail
paths; unique external/provider identifiers are scoped by
tenant/provider; aggregate version supports optimistic concurrency.

Published events: workflow.published, workflow.started,
workflow.step.failed, workflow.completed, workflow.replayed. Consumed
dependencies: DAT-01, IAM-03, ENG-02, AUT-02; dependencies are accessed
by stable contracts/projections, never direct write-table joins.

Failure/degraded behavior: Write commands fail atomically; asynchronous
effects retry idempotently; stale read models carry freshness and cannot
authorize a consequence-bearing mutation beyond budget.

Security/privacy: classification is enforced at field/resource level;
tenant context and authorization are mandatory. Restricted data follows
§21 controls; support/break-glass access creates delegated actor
evidence.

SLI/SLO: Surface/domain API 99.9% initial target; p95 \<500-750 ms by
workload; queue/projection freshness per §12.5.

Eligibility via roster upload, HRIS/API, email domain, code or
enterprise identity.

Employee invitation, self-enrollment, dependent rules, location access
and plan selection.

Joiner, mover and leaver synchronization with grace and conversion to
personal membership.

Consolidated invoice, employee copay, adjustments, credits and
reconciliation.

Privacy-preserving aggregate utilization, engagement, attendance and
program-outcome reporting.

Corporate challenges, events, communications and support contacts.

### Critical Controls

Employers receive only contractually permitted aggregate data.

Individual health, coaching and sensitive activity remains private
unless explicitly authorized.

### Required Outcomes

Enterprise contracts are operable without manual spreadsheets.

Corporate customers can prove utilization and value while protecting
employees.

### Technical Realization Notes

Authority & storage: product-plane PostgreSQL app schema. Authoritative
aggregates are CorporateAccount, CorporateContract, BenefitPlan,
EligibilityRoster, EmployeeEnrollment, EmployerInvoice and
CorporateReport. Contract and eligibility versions are effective-dated;
reporting projections never become membership or billing authority.

Command inventory: CreateCorporateAccount, StartCorporateContract,
AmendBenefitPlan, ImportEligibilityRoster, UpsertEligibility,
InviteEmployee, EnrollEmployee, EndEligibility,
ApplyEligibilityGraceOrConversion, IssueEmployerInvoice,
ApplyEmployerAdjustment, ReconcileEmployerInvoice,
GenerateCorporateReport. Every mutation carries tenant/employer scope,
idempotency and expected aggregate version where stateful.

Queries/read models: CorporateAccountDetail, ContractAndBenefitPlan,
EligibilityRosterStatus, EnrollmentQueue, EmployerBillingSummary,
ReconciliationStatus and PrivacyPreservingUtilizationReport for
Corporate Portal/Admin/Member self-enrollment. Aggregate reports expose
cohort/privacy thresholds and freshness metadata.

Indexes/concurrency: unique (tenant_id, corporate_account_id,
external_employee_id) where supplied; non-overlapping effective
eligibility windows per employee/benefit plan; contract and roster
imports use optimistic versioning; enrollment uses idempotent source
mappings so roster/API retries cannot create duplicate memberships.

Published events: corporate.contract.started, eligibility.added,
employee.enrolled, employee.eligibility.ended, corporate.invoice.issued.
Consumed dependencies: PPL-02, COM-01, COM-03, IAM-01, DAT-02 through
stable contracts/projections; no direct cross-domain write-table joins.

Failure/degraded behavior: HRIS/roster sync failure does not silently
revoke active eligibility; policy-defined grace preserves current access
until an authoritative leaver/effective-end is reconciled. Enrollment
and employer invoicing retry idempotently. Billing or eligibility
divergence opens a reconciliation case rather than rewriting history.

Security/privacy: employer users see only contractually permitted
employee fields and aggregate utilization. Health, coaching, nutrition
and sensitive activity remain inaccessible unless a separately
authorized purpose permits them. Export/report queries enforce tenant +
corporate-account scope and minimum cohort/privacy thresholds.

SLI/SLO: Enterprise corporate-portal and admin APIs target 99.9% monthly
availability; enrollment/eligibility mutation p95 \<500 ms excluding
upstream HRIS; roster-sync and billing projection freshness budgets are
explicit and surfaced when stale.

Tests/runbook: property tests cover eligibility effective windows,
duplicate roster retries, leaver grace/conversion and employer-invoice
reconciliation; privacy tests prove individual Restricted records cannot
leak into employer reports. Runbook RB-B2B-01 covers roster/HRIS outage,
eligibility divergence, enrollment duplication and employer-invoice
reconciliation without history rewrite.

  -----------------------------------------------------

Give large operators centralized governance and comparable insight while
preserving local execution.

### Required Capabilities Preserved

Hierarchy for holding company, brand, franchisee, region, location and
department.

Central standards with inherited/local overrides for catalog, pricing,
membership, brand, access and operations.

Cross-location member access, home club, revenue attribution, transfer
and data ownership policy.

Comparable scorecards and exception queues for revenue, churn,
conversion, NPS, staffing, maintenance and compliance.

Franchise royalty, marketing fund, shared services, intercompany
allocation and settlement exports.

Location opening/closing playbooks, readiness gates and configuration
templates.

Benchmarking with normalized metrics and permissions by hierarchy scope.

### Critical Controls

Local overrides are explicit, bounded and reviewable.

Cross-location analytics use governed definitions and ownership rules.

### Required Outcomes

Head office sees the chain as one operating system.

Local managers retain autonomy within approved guardrails.

### Technical Realization Notes

Authority & storage: product-plane PostgreSQL app schema. Authoritative
aggregates are FranchiseNetwork, Franchisee, GovernanceTemplate,
Override, HomeClub, IntercompanyAllocation and RoyaltyStatement.
Governance/override policy is effective-dated and hierarchy-scoped;
analytics are derived projections.

Command inventory: CreateFranchiseNetwork, RegisterFranchisee,
PublishGovernanceTemplate, RequestLocationOverride,
ApproveLocationOverride, ChangeMemberHomeClub,
RecordIntercompanyAllocation, GenerateRoyaltyStatement,
CloseRoyaltyPeriod, OpenLocationReadiness, CloseLocation. Commands
enforce hierarchy scope, effective version and approval policy.

Queries/read models: NetworkHierarchy, EffectiveGovernanceByLocation,
OverrideRegistry, LocationExceptionQueue,
CrossLocationMemberAccessSummary, HomeClubHistory,
ComparableLocationScorecard, RoyaltyStatementDetail and
IntercompanySettlementSummary. Projections expose metric-definition and
freshness versions.

Indexes/concurrency: hierarchy-node paths and location scope are
tenant-leading; only one effective governance template version per
scope/time window; overrides reference the inherited policy version they
replace; home-club changes are serialized per member; royalty statements
are unique per franchisee/period/version and immutable after close
except append-only correction.

Published events: governance.published, location.exception.detected,
member.home_club.changed, royalty.statement.created. Consumed
dependencies: PLT-01, PLT-02, INT-01, COM-04, IAM-03 through stable
contracts/projections; finance corrections post through COM-04 rather
than mutating closed royalty history.

Failure/degraded behavior: a stale governance projection cannot
authorize a new local override; the caller re-reads the authoritative
effective policy. Cross-location analytics may show stale status but
never drive access/billing mutations. Royalty generation is idempotent
and reconciliation failures open a case instead of rewriting a closed
period.

Security/privacy: hierarchy scope is part of every authorization
decision. Franchise users see only permitted brands/regions/locations;
cross-location member detail follows the underlying
member/health/finance policies rather than franchise role alone.
Governance and override approvals are fully audited.

SLI/SLO: Enterprise franchise/admin APIs target 99.9% monthly
availability; governance reads p95 \<500 ms; cross-location scorecards
may use an explicit analytics freshness budget and cannot authorize
consequence-bearing actions.

Tests/runbook: property tests cover policy inheritance/override
precedence, home-club serialization, royalty allocation balancing,
closed-period immutability and hierarchy authorization. Runbook
RB-B2B-02 covers governance projection drift, invalid overrides,
home-club conflict and royalty/intercompany reconciliation.

Make Veyro an extensible platform with secure, stable and observable
integration contracts.

### Required Capabilities Preserved

Versioned public APIs with consistent resources, pagination, filtering,
errors and idempotency.

OAuth 2/OIDC applications, tenant authorization, granular scopes, API
keys and service accounts.

Webhook subscriptions, event filtering, signing, retries, ordering
guidance, replay and delivery logs.

Sandbox tenant, test data, simulated providers and safe webhook endpoint
testing.

Developer portal with documentation, examples, SDKs, changelog, status
and support.

Rate limits, quotas, usage analytics, error diagnostics and credential
rotation.

API versioning, compatibility, deprecation, migration guides and
contract tests.

Partner certification and security review for sensitive scopes.

### Critical Controls

API authorization is tenant-bound and scope-limited.

Backward compatibility and deprecation windows are contractual product
commitments.

### Required Outcomes

Partners integrate without private documentation or manual credential
exchange.

Integrations are observable and supportable by tenant and partner.

### Technical Realization Notes

Authority & storage: Product PostgreSQL app schema with module-prefixed
authoritative tables; no cross-domain write-table access. Authoritative
entities/tables are DeveloperApp, OAuthGrant, APIKey, Scope,
WebhookSubscription, WebhookDelivery, SandboxTenant, SDKVersion.

Command inventory: CreateAPIApp, GrantScope, RotateClientSecret,
RegisterWebhook, DeliverWebhook, ReplayPublicWebhook,
CreateSandboxTenant. Every command declares permission, idempotency,
expected aggregate version and transaction boundary.

Queries/read models: List/detail and history projections for
DeveloperApp, OAuthGrant, APIKey, Scope; role/surface-specific
attention/summary read models for Developer Portal; Admin Web; Internal
SaaS Console; every projection exposes freshness/version metadata when
asynchronously built.

Indexes/concurrency: tenant-leading indexes for primary list/detail
paths; unique external/provider identifiers are scoped by
tenant/provider; aggregate version supports optimistic concurrency.

Published events: developer_app.created, oauth.granted,
api.rate_limited, webhook.delivered, webhook.failed,
api.version.deprecated. Consumed dependencies: IAM-01, IAM-03, DAT-01,
REL-01; dependencies are accessed by stable contracts/projections, never
direct write-table joins.

Failure/degraded behavior: Write commands fail atomically; asynchronous
effects retry idempotently; stale read models carry freshness and cannot
authorize a consequence-bearing mutation beyond budget.

Security/privacy: classification is enforced at field/resource level;
tenant context and authorization are mandatory. Restricted data follows
§21 controls; support/break-glass access creates delegated actor
evidence.

SLI/SLO: Surface/domain API 99.9% initial target; p95 \<500-750 ms by
workload; queue/projection freshness per §12.5.

Tests/runbook: invariant/property tests for each state transition;
contract tests for APIs/events; tenant isolation negative test where
tenant-owned; runbook RB-ECO-01 covers stuck commands, reconciliation,
provider/dependency outage and repair without history rewrite.

                         applies to mutable/queryable
                         rows.

  Data classification    Confidential/tenant-scoped

  Continuity tier        Tier 1

  Technical interface    Domain command/query
                         interface; no direct table
                         access.

  Async/workflow         Transactional outbox for
  contract               state changes; idempotent
                         consumers.

  Implementation slice   Foundation
  ---------------------------------------------------

Capture every important business state change as a durable, governed and
replayable event.

### Required Capabilities Preserved

Canonical event envelope with tenant, aggregate, actor, correlation,
causation, schema, timestamp and source.

Transactional outbox or equivalent guarantee between state change and
event publication.

Schema registry, compatibility rules, ownership, classification and
deprecation.

At-least-once delivery with idempotent consumers, retry, dead-letter and
replay.

Event routing to timeline, automation, notification, analytics,
integrations, fraud and AI.

Retention, compaction, PII minimization, encryption and regional
routing.

Operational explorer for correlation tracing and controlled replay.

Business event catalog accessible to product, engineering, analytics and
partners.

### Critical Controls

Events contain only data needed by approved consumers and preserve
tenant boundaries.

Schema changes follow compatibility and consumer migration policy.

### Required Outcomes

Analytics, automation and integrations react consistently to the same
truth.

Complex workflows are traceable across services and channels.

### Technical Realization Notes

Authority & storage: Product PostgreSQL audit/app tables + classified S3
evidence/archive; tenant RLS applies to mutable/queryable rows.
Authoritative entities/tables are DomainEvent, EventSchema,
OutboxRecord, Subscription, ConsumerCheckpoint, DeadLetterEvent,
ReplayJob.

Command inventory: AppendOutboxEvent, PublishBusinessEvent,
RegisterEventSchema, DeprecateEventSchema, ReplayProjection,
QuarantineDelivery, ArchiveEvent. Every command declares permission,
idempotency, expected aggregate version and transaction boundary.

Queries/read models: List/detail and history projections for
DomainEvent, EventSchema, OutboxRecord, Subscription;
role/surface-specific attention/summary read models for Platform;
Developer Portal; Internal SaaS Console; every projection exposes
freshness/version metadata when asynchronously built.

Indexes/concurrency: tenant/aggregate/time and unpublished-outbox
indexes; event_id globally unique; dispatched-at state does not change
business payload.

Published events: event.delivery.failed, event.replayed,
event_schema.changed. Consumed dependencies: PLT-01, SEC-01, REL-01;
dependencies are accessed by stable contracts/projections, never direct
write-table joins. Direction for this intentional bidirectional pair
(DAT-01 \<-\> REL-01) is normative in §6.3.

Failure/degraded behavior: Write commands fail atomically; asynchronous
effects retry idempotently; stale read models carry freshness and cannot
authorize a consequence-bearing mutation beyond budget.

Security/privacy: classification is enforced at field/resource level;
tenant context and authorization are mandatory. Restricted data follows
§21 controls; support/break-glass access creates delegated actor
evidence.

SLI/SLO: Tier-1 control path 99.95%+; policy/tenant resolution p95 \<100
ms in-process/cache where applicable; zero cross-tenant/privileged
control breaches.

Tests/runbook: invariant/property tests for each state transition;
contract tests for APIs/events; tenant isolation negative test where
tenant-owned; runbook RB-DAT-01 covers stuck commands, reconciliation,
provider/dependency outage and repair without history rewrite.

Security architecture, threat modeling, secure defaults, least privilege
and zero-trust service identity.

vault and certificate lifecycle.

Secure SDLC with code review, SAST/DAST, dependency, container, IaC and
secret scanning.

Vulnerability management, penetration tests, bug response, risk
acceptance and remediation SLAs.

biometrics, media and data sharing with version history.

and deletion with identity and legal checks.

subprocessor governance.

Security monitoring, incident response, evidence, notification
assessment and postmortem.

controls evidence and questionnaire response.

### Critical Controls

Privacy and security review is mandatory for biometric, health, AI and
new data-sharing capabilities.

Production access is just-in-time, purpose-bound and audited.

### Required Outcomes

Security becomes a sales enabler and operational discipline.

Users retain meaningful control over sensitive data.

Keep critical club and SaaS operations available, recoverable and
communicable under component, provider, network or regional failure.

### Required Capabilities Preserved

Service-level indicators, objectives and error budgets for login,
access, booking, POS, payments, messaging and core APIs.

Resilient patterns: timeout, retry with jitter, circuit breaker,
bulkhead, queue, idempotency and graceful degradation.

Offline modes for check-in, access and selected front-desk/POS
operations with bounded risk and reconciliation.

Backup, point-in-time recovery, restore testing, replication and
tenant-level recovery procedures.

Documented RPO/RTO by data and workflow criticality.

Disaster recovery for zone, region, database, object storage, queue and
identity dependencies.

Incident command, severity, ownership, timeline, runbook, status page,
customer communication and postmortem.

Provider continuity plans for payments, messaging, access hardware,
biometric and cloud services.

Chaos, failover, restore and business-continuity drills on a defined
cadence.

### Critical Controls

Critical workflows define explicit degraded behavior rather than fail
unpredictably.

Backups are not considered valid until restore drills pass.

### Required Outcomes

Gyms continue core operation during common outages.

Incidents are detected, contained, communicated and learned from.

### Technical Realization Notes

Authority & storage: Product PostgreSQL app schema with module-prefixed
authoritative tables; no cross-domain write-table access. Authoritative

Regional recovery uses Bahrain primary/UAE warm DR, measured replication
lag and the PITR reconciliation runbook; aspirational RPO/RTO is never
reported as met without a drill.

Failure/degraded behavior: Fail closed for privileged/restricted

evidence.
