# 11. API, BFF & Realtime Contract

## 11.1 API Style

### Idempotency contract

Mutation idempotency scope is (tenant_id, HTTP method, canonical route,
Idempotency-Key). Keys are retained for at least 24 hours and longer for
payments/fiscal/provider operations according to provider retry windows.

The server stores request hash, authoritative result/status, response
body reference and expiry. Reuse with the same body returns the stored
response and original status; reuse with a different body returns HTTP
409 with code IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED_WITH_DIFFERENT_PAYLOAD.

The same idempotency key becomes command_id and is propagated to
outbox/provider dispatch records. Provider-specific idempotency keys are
deterministic derivatives rather than newly generated values.

Versioned REST/JSON external and application APIs under /api/v1. OpenAPI
is the contract source for generated clients.

Commands are explicit action endpoints when domain semantics matter (for
example /memberships/{id}:freeze) rather than generic PATCH for
consequence-heavy transitions.

Queries use resource endpoints and surface-specific read endpoints for
Member 360, Command Center, Coach Today and other composed views.

Cursor pagination for large changing collections; offset pagination
allowed only for small stable reference data.

RFC 7807 Problem Details-compatible error envelope with stable machine
code, localized safe message, correlation ID and recoverability
metadata.

Idempotency-Key required for externally retryable mutations such as
orders, payments, refunds, booking, check-in and workflow starts.

ETag/resource version or expected_version used for optimistic
concurrency on user-edited records.

Every response that is time-sensitive may include
generated_at/data_freshness metadata; AI/analytics responses must expose
source freshness.

  ---------------------------------------------
  **POST
  /api/v1/memberships/{membership_id}:freeze\
  Headers:\
  Authorization: Bearer \...\
  Idempotency-Key: \<uuid\>\
  X-Request-ID: \<uuid\>\
  Body:\
  { effective_date, reason_code,
  requested_end_date? }\
  \
  Response 202:\
  { operation_id, membership_id, state:
  \"freeze_scheduled\", version }\**
  ---------------------------------------------

  ---------------------------------------------

## 11.2 BFF Rules

Admin BFF composes permission-filtered business views; it does not own
authoritative state.

Coach BFF is relationship-aware and returns only assigned/permitted
clients and health context.

Member BFF returns the signed-in member/household context and hides
internal operational fields.

Front Desk BFF prioritizes low-latency lookup/access/payment and
supports degraded cache hints.

Internal Console BFF is a separate privileged application boundary;
customer content access requires temporary support session policy.

## 11.3 Realtime

WebSocket/SSE is used for live arrivals, conversation updates, async job
progress, POS/provider state and operational incident status.

Realtime channels are authorized per tenant/user/resource and carry no
state that cannot be reconstructed from authoritative storage/events.

Reconnect uses last_event_id/sequence where possible; clients must
tolerate missed realtime and refresh authoritative state.

## 11.4 Public API and Webhooks (V2-ready)

OAuth 2.1/OIDC authorization for partner apps; service accounts/API keys
only for approved server-to-server use cases.

Scopes are tenant-authorized and domain-specific. Sensitive scopes
require partner certification and tenant admin consent.

Webhooks are HMAC-signed, timestamped and replay-protected; retries use
exponential backoff, delivery logs and controlled replay.

Public webhook delivery is unordered unless a specific public contract
explicitly guarantees otherwise. Payloads carry resource/version
metadata; consumers must deduplicate and reconcile from the current
resource state rather than infer state from arrival order.

API deprecation includes announced sunset, compatibility tests and
migration guidance.

## 11.5 Stable Error Catalog

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Code**                                         **HTTP**  **Meaning**
  ----------------------------------------------- ---------- ------------------------
  TENANT_CONTEXT_MISSING                           401/403   No validated tenant
                                                             context.

  TENANT_SCOPE_MISMATCH                              403     Resource belongs to
                                                             another scope.

  PERMISSION_DENIED                                  403     Action/resource/scope
                                                             denied.

  ASSURANCE_REQUIRED                                 403     Step-up authentication
                                                             required.

  APPROVAL_REQUIRED                                  409     Action awaits approval.

  IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED_WITH_DIFFERENT_PAYLOAD      409     Same key, different
                                                             request hash.

  VERSION_CONFLICT                                   409     Optimistic-concurrency
                                                             conflict.

  INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION                           409     Aggregate state does not
                                                             allow transition.

  ENTITLEMENT_NOT_AVAILABLE                          409     No usable entitlement.

  ENTITLEMENT_RESERVATION_CONFLICT                   409     Grant is
                                                             reserved/consumed
                                                             elsewhere.

  CAPACITY_UNAVAILABLE                               409     Schedule capacity
                                                             exhausted.

  PAYMENT_PROVIDER_PENDING                           202     Provider outcome not
                                                             final.

  PAYMENT_FAILED                                     402     Provider or instrument
                                                             failure.

  FISCALIZATION_UNAVAILABLE                          503     Required fiscal provider
                                                             unavailable.

  OFFLINE_OPERATION_NOT_ALLOWED                      409     Operation cannot
                                                             legally/safely complete
                                                             offline.

  ACCESS_DENIED                                      403     Policy/entitlement
                                                             decision denied.

  ACCESS_SNAPSHOT_STALE                              503     Offline snapshot beyond
                                                             permitted age.

  CONSENT_REQUIRED                                   409     Required consent
                                                             missing/expired.

  DATA_RESTRICTED                                    403     Field/resource
                                                             restricted by privacy
                                                             policy.

  RATE_LIMITED                                       429     Operation/tenant/user
                                                             rate limit exceeded.

  DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE                             503     External/internal
                                                             dependency unavailable.

  PROJECTION_STALE                                   503     Read model too stale to
                                                             authorize
                                                             consequence-bearing
                                                             action.

  VALIDATION_FAILED                                  422     Typed field/business
                                                             validation errors.

  NOT_FOUND                                          404     Resource not visible or
                                                             not found.

  CONFLICT_REQUIRES_REVIEW                           409     Offline/import conflict
                                                             requires human review.
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 11.6 Masked Field Representation and Cache Safety

ALLOW_MASKED returns the same resource shape but sensitive fields use a
typed object {value:null, visibility:\"masked\",
mask_reason:\<stable-code\>} or a field-level metadata map generated by
the BFF. APIs never substitute misleading fake values.

Authorization_variant (full\|masked\|summary) and policy_version are
part of BFF/read-model cache keys. A cache entry created for a masked
caller cannot satisfy an unmasked request, and vice versa.

OpenAPI schemas annotate maskable fields and SDKs expose a Masked\<T\>
wrapper for strongly typed clients.

## 11.7 Public Webhook Contract Projection

Public webhooks are a separate versioned contract, not raw internal
events. Internal events are projected to stable public event
names/payloads after tenant scope, data classification and partner scope
filtering.

Webhook payloads include public_event_id, tenant_id, type, occurred_at,
resource reference, version and minimal public data.
Restricted/health/biometric fields are never exported without an
explicit product scope and tenant authorization.

Signing uses rotating asymmetric/HMAC secrets per app, retry uses
exponential backoff, and delivery dedupe is keyed by public_event_id +
endpoint. Partner replay uses the public event store rather than
replaying internal consumers.

## 11.8 UX Screen-to-BFF Contract Manifest

The approved 170-screen registry is integrated through a
machine-readable contracts/ui/screen-contracts.yaml artifact rather than
duplicated manually in this document. CI requires one row per V1 Screen
ID and rejects orphan/missing screens before feature implementation.

Each row declares screen_id, surface, primary_query/read_model,
mutation_commands, realtime_topics, required_permissions,
masking_variant, offline_behavior and error/state codes. The manifest is
generated/validated against the canonical design registry and
OpenAPI/AsyncAPI contracts.

Representative bindings: Admin Command Center →
/bff/admin/command-center read model + attention/AI action commands;
Member 360 → /bff/admin/members/{id}/360; Coach Today →
/bff/coach/today; Member Home → /bff/member/home; Front Desk live
arrivals → /bff/front-desk/arrivals. Exact Screen IDs remain sourced
from the canonical UX registry to prevent hand-maintained drift.

# 12. Event Architecture & Asynchronous Processing

![Figure 2. State-to-event consistency and idempotent delivery
model.](media/image2.png "Figure 2. State-to-event consistency and idempotent delivery model."){width="6.75in"
height="0.6106310148731409in"}

*Figure 2. State-to-event consistency and idempotent delivery model.*

## 12.1 Canonical Event Envelope

  --------------------------------------------
  **{\
  \"event_id\": \"uuidv7\",\
  \"event_type\": \"membership.activated\",\
  \"schema_version\": 1,\
  \"occurred_at\": \"UTC instant\",\
  \"published_at\": \"UTC instant\",\
  \"tenant_id\": \"\...\",\
  \"organization_id\": \"\...\",\
  \"brand_id\": \"\...\",\
  \"location_id\": \"\...\",\
  \"aggregate_type\": \"Membership\",\
  \"aggregate_id\": \"\...\",\
  \"aggregate_version\": 7,\
  \"actor\": { \"type\":
  \"user\|service\|delegated\", \"id\":
  \"\...\", \"assurance\": \"AAL-2\" },\
  \"correlation_id\": \"\...\",\
  \"causation_id\": \"\...\",\
  \"idempotency_key\": \"\...\",\
  \"classification\": \"confidential\",\
  \"purpose\": \"membership_sale\",\
  \"region\": \"\...\",\
  \"payload\": { \... }\
  }\**
  --------------------------------------------

  --------------------------------------------

## 12.2 Publication and Consumption

### Replay and external side-effect safety

Consumers declare one of REPLAY_SAFE_PURE,
REPLAY_SAFE_DEDUPED_SIDE_EFFECT or REPLAY_FORBIDDEN. Replays default to
side_effects=suppressed unless an incident commander authorizes a
specific deduped side-effect class.

Messaging/payment/tax/device dispatch writes a DispatchGuard row before
provider invocation using unique (tenant_id, event_id, channel/action,
recipient/resource). Provider callbacks reconcile the same dispatch
record; a replay cannot create a second provider action.

Projection consumers may replay freely into empty/rebuild stores.
Authorization decisions never rely on a projection whose freshness
exceeds its declared budget.

A domain transaction writes aggregate changes and one or more outbox
records in the same PostgreSQL transaction.

Outbox relay publishes to a domain topic/stream. Publication retries are
safe; outbox rows record broker acknowledgement.

Consumers keep an inbox/deduplication record keyed by event_id and
process idempotently.

Poison events move to DLQ after bounded retries and create an
operational case with tenant impact and replay guidance.

Schema compatibility is enforced in CI. Additive changes are preferred;
breaking changes use a new event schema version and
dual-publish/migration window.

PII is minimized in events. Consumers retrieve restricted detail through
authorized domain APIs rather than copying sensitive payloads broadly.

Timeline projections store user-safe event summaries, not raw event
payloads.

## 12.3 Routing and Consumer Ordering Strategy

Logical routing name: veyro.\<domain\>.\<event-family\>.v1. Physical
queue/topic consolidation is allowed if schema and ownership boundaries
remain explicit.

The V1 EventBridge/SNS + standard SQS transport provides no
delivery-order guarantee, including for events from the same aggregate.
tenant_id + aggregate_id remains correlation/routing metadata only; it
is not an ordering primitive.

Every consumer is order-independent. Projection consumers gate on
aggregate_version: apply only the next expected version, ignore
duplicate/older versions, and on a version gap buffer briefly then
re-read/rebuild from authoritative state or the retained event archive
before marking the projection fresh. Consequence-bearing commands never
authorize from an unresolved-gap projection.

Property and contract tests shuffle, duplicate and delay delivery for
each stateful projection and require convergence to the authoritative
aggregate version. A future FIFO/streaming transport may optimize
ordering but cannot weaken this consumer rule.

Event retention is classification/operational-need driven. Long-term
business history belongs in domain stores/warehouse, not indefinitely in
the queue transport.

## 12.4 Contract Registry and Event Classes

Business domain events are durable, versioned, replayable contracts
produced from the transactional outbox. Analytics/telemetry signals use
a separate pipeline, may be sampled, and never drive authoritative
business state.

Event schemas live in contracts/events as JSON Schema/AsyncAPI with
owner, classification, compatibility mode and deprecation date. CI
performs backward-compatibility checks and rejects any event name
referenced by code/flow documentation but absent from the registry.

V1 transport is EventBridge/SNS + consumer SQS. Event archive in S3
stores the canonical envelope for controlled historical rebuild.
Kafka-compatible transport is introduced only when sustained
throughput/replay requirements cross the extraction threshold.

## 12.5 Queue, Lag and DLQ Objectives

  --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Class**       **Freshness/Lag SLO** **Alert**        **DLQ/Error
                                                         Budget**
  --------------- --------------------- ---------------- -------------------
  Tier-1 command  \<30 s p95 queue age  \<5 min          DLQ = 0 tolerated
  side effects                          oldest-message   for
                                        alert            financial/access
                                                         until triaged

  Operational     \<60 s p95 freshness  \<5 min alert    DLQ \<0.01% daily
  projections                                            

  Notifications   \<2 min p95           \<10 min alert   Provider-specific
                  request-to-dispatch                    retry budget

  Analytics       \<15 min p95          \<60 min alert   Loss budget
  telemetry       freshness                              documented by
                                                         signal
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 13. Durable Workflows, Tasks & Approvals

## 13.1 When to Use a Workflow

A process spans multiple domains and cannot complete in one local
transaction.

A provider callback/timer/human approval may arrive minutes or days
later.

Compensation/retry must survive process restarts or deployments.

A business SLA/escalation must be visible and auditable.

Examples: tenant provisioning, membership activation with external
payment, dunning, migration, offboarding, refund, incident
communications, app release, data deletion request.

## 13.2 Workflow Rules

Workflow state is durable and versioned. Workflow code changes use
deterministic versioning/patch markers.

Activities are idempotent and may run more than once. External provider
requests carry stable idempotency references.

Human approvals are domain records linked to workflow state; an approval
result cannot be inferred from a notification click alone.

Compensation is explicit. Never "rollback" a completed payment by
deleting records; issue a refund/reversal command.

Timers use workflow engine time, not ad-hoc cron rows. Cron remains for
simple stateless maintenance only.

Every workflow exposes current state, next wait condition, attempts,
last error and recovery action to support tooling.

## 13.3 Workflow Tenant Isolation and Privacy

Every workflow ID and search attribute carries tenant_id and
workflow_type. A workflow may only invoke activities through a
TenantContext created from its validated start command; cross-tenant
signal/query APIs are rejected.

Restricted PII/health/payment data is not embedded in workflow
input/history. Histories store opaque resource IDs, command hashes and
non-sensitive status. Activities fetch current authorized data at
execution time.

History retention is bounded by workflow/legal need and must not exceed
the privacy retention schedule. Dunning/provisioning/migration workflows
checkpoint durable domain state so recovery does not depend on an
indefinitely retained orchestration history.

# 14. Commerce, Billing, Payments, Ledger & POS

![Figure 3. Financial and membership coordination without collapsing
distinct sources of
truth.](media/image3.png "Figure 3. Financial and membership coordination without collapsing distinct sources of truth."){width="6.75in"
height="0.6595527121609799in"}

*Figure 3. Financial and membership coordination without collapsing
distinct sources of truth.*

## 14.1 Money and Tax

Use integer minor units plus ISO currency. JOD is represented in fils,
preserving three decimal places; no binary floating point in business
logic.

Price, discount, tax and exchange results are resolved into immutable
order/invoice line snapshots with source policy/version.

Tax rules are regional configuration/providers; tax rate is never
globally hard-coded.

Rounding policy is explicit by currency/tax jurisdiction and tested with
boundary cases.

## 14.2 Payment State Machine

  --------------------------------------------
  **created -\> requires_action? -\>
  authorized -\> captured -\> succeeded\
  -\> failed\
  -\> cancelled\
  succeeded -\> partially_refunded -\>
  refunded\
  succeeded -\> disputed/chargeback -\>
  resolved\**
  --------------------------------------------

  --------------------------------------------

Provider redirect/UI state is not authoritative. Signed provider webhook
or verified provider query drives final payment state.

PaymentIntent stores provider adapter, provider reference, amount,
currency, customer/payment token reference and idempotency key.

Card PAN/CVV is never stored by Veyro. Prefer hosted
fields/tokenization/terminal flows to minimize PCI scope.

All provider callbacks are authenticated, timestamp-checked,
replay-protected and deduplicated.

Retries never create a second economic charge because both Veyro and
provider calls use stable idempotency keys.

## 14.3 Ledger

### Deferred revenue and recognition

Prepaid membership cash posts to cash/provider-clearing and
UnearnedMembershipRevenue. Revenue is recognized over the service period
according to an immutable RevenueRecognitionSchedule linked to
membership/invoice lines.

Service/PT credits post initially to ServiceCreditLiability and
recognize revenue on consumption or policy-defined expiry/forfeiture.
Wallet top-ups remain WalletLiability until applied.

Freeze extends or pauses recognition according to contract policy;
cancellation/upgrade/downgrade computes earned vs unearned through the
effective date, posts refund/credit/contra entries and creates a
replacement recognition schedule. Posted recognition entries are never
rewritten.

Proration calculates in high precision, allocates tax/discount at line
level, then rounds using the currency exponent (JOD = 3 decimal minor
units). Sum-of-parts reconciliation must equal invoice/ledger totals.

Double-entry journal with immutable JournalEntry and Posting rows. A
journal entry must balance per currency.

Business subledgers: member receivable, cash, provider clearing,
revenue, tax payable, wallet liability, service-credit liability,
refunds/contra revenue, inventory COGS where enabled.

Wallet/service credits are liabilities or contractual credits, not
mutable balance columns. Current balance is a projection.

Correction uses reversal/compensating journal entry referencing the
original; no update/delete of posted financial entries.

Provider settlement imports reconcile provider clearing to
bank/settlement data; mismatches create cases, never silent balance
edits.

## 14.4 Membership Sale Transaction Boundary

Resolve product/price/tax/promotion and create an Order with immutable
commercial snapshot.

Create/finalize Invoice according to billing schedule.

Create PaymentIntent and call provider outside DB transaction.

On confirmed payment, record Payment and post Ledger journal
idempotently.

Membership command activates agreement and emits membership.activated.

Entitlement projection/grants update; access/member app/search/timeline
react asynchronously.

If downstream entitlement/index notification fails, payment/membership
truth remains correct and replayable.

## 14.5 POS and Offline

### Jordan fiscal completion rule

A Veyro order number/local offline receipt is not a Jordan tax invoice.
For Jordan tenants, the sale state differentiates ORDER_ACCEPTED,
PAYMENT_PENDING, FISCAL_PENDING and FISCAL_COMPLETE.

Until ISTD explicitly validates an offline fiscal procedure for Veyro, a
terminal may build a cart and preserve an OfflineSaleDraft, but final
tax-invoice completion and payment capture that legally requires
immediate invoicing are fail-closed when JoFotara is unavailable. The UI
must not display "paid/fiscal complete".

Server fiscal serials are unique per legal entity/series and stored with
provider UUID/reference/QR acknowledgement. Credit notes/returns
reference the original fiscal document and are idempotent. Any future
preallocated serial-block mechanism requires written tax validation and
a dedicated ADR before enablement.

## 14.6 Revenue Recognition and Period Close

A scheduled accounting job posts recognition entries by legal
entity/accounting date and is idempotent per schedule period. Period
close freezes normal back-dated postings; late corrections use
controlled adjustment journals into an open period with reference to the
original event.

Financial reports expose cash collected, receivable, unearned revenue,
earned revenue, tax liability, provider clearing and
wallet/service-credit liabilities separately. Revenue is never inferred
directly from successful payments.

## 14.7 Functional Currency and FX

Each LegalEntity has one functional currency. Every monetary posting
stores transaction_currency, amount_minor/high-precision amount,
functional_currency, functional_amount and fx_rate_snapshot_id when
currencies differ.

FxRateSnapshot records source, rate, quote/base convention, effective
timestamp and retrieval evidence; rates are immutable once referenced.
Settlement differences post to realized FX gain/loss. Open foreign
receivables/payables may be revalued at period close with reversing
entries.

Jordan V1 operates JOD functional currency and may restrict
sellable/payment instruments to JOD until a tenant explicitly enables a
validated multi-currency policy. The model remains multi-currency ready
without silently converting values.

Front Desk/POS maintains a local bounded cart and product snapshot. The
server owns order numbers, final pricing policy and financial posting.

Offline cash sales may be queued within configured limits only for
non-fiscal tenders/markets or where the applicable regional fiscal
policy explicitly permits provisional offline sale capture. For Jordan
fiscal transactions, §14.5/§26 fail-closed fiscalization rules prevail.
Provider-dependent card payments are only "paid" if the
terminal/provider confirms supported offline capture; otherwise state is
"payment pending".

Cash shift open/close, expected cash, counted cash and variance are
explicit records with role/approval thresholds.

Inventory reservation/fulfillment is linked to order lines and
reconciled if offline stock state conflicts.

# 15. Memberships, Entitlements, Scheduling & Booking

## 15.1 Membership Lifecycle

Membership stores agreement terms/version, start/end, renewal mode,
lifecycle state and billing relationship. It never derives access by
itself.

Freeze/resume/upgrade/downgrade/cancel/transfer are explicit commands
with effective dates, policy evaluation, billing/proration effects and
audit.

Historical terms and past periods are immutable; future scheduled
changes are separate records.

Dunning may suspend entitlement according to policy without destroying
membership history.

## 15.2 Entitlement Engine

### Authoritative MemberEntitlementGrant state machine

COM-01 owns MemberEntitlementGrant(source_type/source_id, member_id,
entitlement_type, quantity/unlimited, valid_from/to, location/resource
scope, policy_version, version). PLT-03 uses PlanEntitlement for Veyro
SaaS plan packaging; the terms are never interchangeable.

Finite grants use atomic RESERVED → CONSUMED or RESERVED → RELEASED
transitions. Reserve records reservation_id, purpose/resource, expiry
and idempotency_key; a unique active reservation/remaining-quantity
constraint plus optimistic version update prevents double spend.

Events: entitlement.granted, entitlement.reserved, entitlement.consumed,
entitlement.released, entitlement.expired, entitlement.revoked. Booking
reserves where policy requires; session/access fulfilment consumes;
cancellation releases. Expired reservations are released by an
idempotent worker.

COM-04 ServiceCredit is the accounting liability/recognition source.
COM-01 grant is authoritative for "may this member use the service now?"
Reconciliation compares grant consumption to service-credit financial
postings and opens a case on mismatch.

  --------------------------------------------
  **evaluate(subject, capability, location,
  resource?, at_time, context)\
  -\> ALLOW \| DENY \| REQUIRE_PAYMENT \|
  REQUIRE_BOOKING \| LIMIT_REACHED\
  + reason_code + policy_version +
  remaining_quantity?\**
  --------------------------------------------

  --------------------------------------------

Entitlement grants may originate from membership, package, corporate
eligibility, promotion, manual approved grant or service credit.

Quantitative entitlements use a reservation/consume/release model for PT
sessions, classes, guest passes and limited services.

Access, booking and POS query the entitlement service rather than
interpreting membership plan codes.

Entitlement decisions are time- and location-aware and retain the
policy/grant version used.

## 15.3 Scheduling and Booking

Schedule owns published occurrences/resources/capacity. Booking owns
member reservation/waitlist/cancel/attendance intent.

Capacity changes use optimistic concurrency or atomic reservation
counters to prevent overbooking.

Booking create evaluates eligibility, entitlement, booking window,
cancellation/no-show policy and resource capacity.

Waitlist promotion is an idempotent workflow with offer/expiry policy; a
member cannot consume the same capacity twice.

Recurring schedule definition is separate from generated occurrences so
historical instances remain stable after template edits.

Time zones are location-specific; store UTC instants and source local
timezone/recurrence rule for correct DST behavior.

# 16. Access Control, Biometrics, Edge & Offline Operation

![Figure 4. Online and bounded offline access decision
path.](media/image4.png "Figure 4. Online and bounded offline access decision path."){width="6.75in"
height="0.7526902887139107in"}

*Figure 4. Online and bounded offline access decision path.*

## 16.1 Credential vs Authorization

QR, NFC, wallet pass, physical card and biometric token are credentials.
They identify a subject/credential record; they do not encode
unrestricted authorization.

Access decision evaluates credential status, subject identity,
location/zone, time, entitlement, membership policy, anti-passback,
suspension and device trust.

Every decision returns stable reason codes suitable for
member/front-desk explanation and stores policy/entitlement version
references.

## 16.2 Edge Agent

### Offline snapshot bounds

Standard access snapshot authorization TTL is 12 hours; high-risk zones
default to 2 hours and may be configured shorter. Online devices request
deltas at least every 5 minutes and immediately on a pushed revocation
epoch.

Snapshot payload target is ≤5 MB per 10,000 active credentials and
contains only pseudonymous credential hashes, minimal entitlement/policy
bits, validity windows and revocation epoch. No member
profile/health/payment history is replicated.

Device signing/encryption keys rotate at least every 90 days and
immediately on compromise/re-provisioning. If device clock skew exceeds
60 seconds, rotating credentials are not accepted; the device enters
supervised/manual degraded mode.

Offline anti-passback is local to a device/connected controller group.
Cross-device global anti-passback is not claimed while disconnected;
reconciliation flags duplicates after reconnect.

Rust service with per-device mTLS certificate and device registration.
Secure update channel and staged rollout.

Local SQLite WAL stores signed access snapshot, device configuration,
command/event queue and last sync markers; no unrestricted member
database replica.

Signed snapshot contains minimal
credential-to-subject/entitlement/policy material with short TTL and
revocation epoch.

Clock integrity is monitored because offline validity windows depend on
time. Large skew moves device into degraded/manual mode.

Offline events carry local monotonic sequence and idempotency key;
reconnect reconciliation deduplicates and flags policy conflicts rather
than rewriting history.

## 16.3 Biometrics

Device Face ID/Touch ID remains OS-local and is used only for app
authentication/step-up.

Facility facial recognition is a separate optional system with explicit
consent, alternative methods, liveness, retention/deletion policy and
vendor-neutral adapter.

Prefer storing encrypted biometric template/token with specialist
vendor/secure boundary rather than raw images; any retained enrollment
media requires explicit purpose/retention.

Biometric match result is an identification signal; final access
authorization still uses Veyro policy/entitlement.

Staff attendance biometric policy is distinct from member access policy
and must be regionally/labor reviewed.

## 16.4 Life-Safety and Emergency Door Behavior

Every access point is commissioned with a hardware safety profile:
fail-safe, fail-secure or mechanical-free-egress according to door type,
fire code, landlord/civil-defence requirements and vendor certification.
Software cannot override required egress behavior.

Egress is never conditioned on Veyro membership, cloud reachability or
software authorization. Maglocks/turnstiles used on an egress path must
have the required fire-alarm/emergency-release wiring outside the Veyro
application path.

Emergency unlock is a distinct privileged command with step-up/dual
approval where time permits, device target, reason, actor and outcome
audit. A local physical emergency input remains available when the
network/edge agent is unavailable.

Commissioning tests power loss, edge-agent crash, controller disconnect,
fire-alarm input, emergency unlock, recovery and manual override. A
failed safety test blocks opening the access point in production.

Occupancy derived from access events is operational/advisory unless both
entry and exit are reliably measured. It is never the sole life-safety
muster source.

## 16.5 Rotating QR / Mobile Credential Anti-Replay

The Member app derives a rotating signed credential token from a
device-bound enrollment secret kept in Keychain/Keystore. Token fields
include credential_id, tenant/location scope, issued_at, expires_at,
rotation counter/nonce and signature; no raw PII is encoded.

Default QR lifetime is 30 seconds with configurable ±30-second reader
clock tolerance. Edge readers validate signature, scope, revocation
epoch and recent-token replay cache before policy evaluation. Online
facilities may share replay evidence through the edge group; offline
protection is bounded to the local controller group.

Screenshot sharing is mitigated by short lifetime and device-bound
rotation, not assumed impossible. Suspected sharing can revoke the
credential/device without changing the member identity.

# 17. Coaching, Training, Nutrition, Health & Safety

## 17.1 Coach Workspace

Coach Today is a permissioned projection over schedule, assigned
clients, overdue attention, sessions and relevant plan state.

Coach-client relationship is explicit and time-bounded; access to
health/nutrition notes follows relationship and field policy.

Session completion and PT credit consumption are separate but
coordinated events; disputed/late verification remains auditable.

## 17.2 Training Versioning and Offline Logging

Program, workout template and exercise prescription are versioned.
Assignment points to an exact version.

WorkoutLog/SetLog is append/update during an active session but final
completion freezes the executed prescription reference.

The shared KMP mobile sync layer may cache assigned workouts and queue
set logs offline on both Android and iOS with client-generated
UUIDv7/idempotency keys; conflict rule favors preserving both
observations and surfacing an edit conflict rather than data loss.

Weights/measurements store numeric value + unit + provenance;
presentation/localization does not alter stored canonical unit
semantics.

## 17.3 Nutrition

### Blocking nutrition constraint validation

MemberNutritionConstraintSet is versioned and distinguishes
allergy/intolerance/religious/preference/clinical-review flags with
source, confidence, effective dates and qualified-review status.

Plan publish, member meal swap and AI-generated suggestion execute the
same blocking validator against the assignment-time constraint version.
Unknown/conflicting allergen data fails closed for the affected
food/recipe and requires a safe alternative or qualified review.

Overrides require an authorized nutrition/clinical role, explicit
reason, member/tenant policy eligibility and immutable audit linking the
exact constraint and plan versions. AI cannot override a blocking
constraint.

Clinical trigger criteria remain supplied by accountable
regional/clinical governance and are versioned policy data; product code
owns routing/enforcement, not medical policy authorship.

NutritionPlan versions targets, meal slots, recipes/foods, alternatives,
constraints and assignment window.

AI/template/manual plan creation converges on the same validated plan
schema.

Meal logging records planned-item linkage or ad-hoc food, quantity,
source (manual/search/barcode/photo estimate), confidence where
estimated and observed time.

Swap suggestions must satisfy the member constraints known to the
system; clinical/qualified-review triggers are policy supplied by
accountable regional/clinical governance, not invented in code or AI
prompts.

Restricted/disabled/review-required nutrition modes are first-class
policy states.

## 17.4 Health and Safety

PAR-Q/screening, limitations, waivers and consent are versioned evidence
records. Current restriction is a projection from authoritative
signed/reviewed records.

Incidents have severity, people, location, time, narrative/evidence,
escalation, corrective action and closure; restricted visibility and
immutable history apply.

Emergency access/break-glass to health context requires purpose,
elevated assurance and audit.

Veyro stores coaching/wellness information but does not claim
diagnosis/treatment. Medical escalation is a policy/workflow boundary.

# 18. Communication, Notifications, Search & Member Timeline

## 18.1 Conversation and Messaging

Conversation is channel-agnostic; Message stores channel/provider
delivery evidence and contextual links to
member/booking/payment/meal/task where permitted.

WhatsApp, SMS, email, push and in-app providers sit behind adapter
interfaces. Provider message IDs and delivery callbacks are
deduplicated.

Consent, quiet hours, channel preference, transactional-vs-marketing
purpose and regional rules are enforced before dispatch.

Inbound messages create/update a conversation and route to assigned
team/coach/inbox through workflow rules.

## 18.2 Notification Orchestrator

Domain event or explicit command creates NotificationRequest with
template version, recipient, purpose, locale, channels and context.

Renderer uses immutable template version and localized variables; no
sensitive data is inserted into channels not approved for that
classification.

Provider retries are bounded; permanent failure updates delivery state
and may trigger fallback channel according to policy.

## 18.3 Global Search

Search index contains permission-aware projections for people, leads,
invoices, payments, bookings, classes, products, staff, help and
commands.

Documents carry tenant_id, scope IDs, classification and visibility
attributes. Query pre-filter is mandatory.

Sensitive search hits are revalidated against domain authorization
before detail is returned.

Index updates are asynchronous from domain events and expose freshness.
Missing/stale index must never allow a mutation without authoritative
re-read.

## 18.4 Member Timeline

Timeline is a projection of selected domain events into human-readable
entries. It is not the source of truth for domain state.

Each timeline item references the authoritative aggregate/event and
applies permission/field masking at read time.

Projection can be rebuilt from retained events/domain history; user
notes/messages remain owned by their source domains.

# 19. Analytics, Data Platform & AI Architecture

## 19.1 Operational Analytics

V1 Command Center and operational metrics use domain read
models/materialized aggregates where freshness requirements are
seconds/minutes.

Metric definitions have owner, SQL/semantic definition, dimensions,
freshness SLA and quality checks; dashboards do not invent metric logic
client-side.

Large historical/cohort/benchmark workloads move to the analytics
platform in V1.5, fed from events/CDC/provider settlements.

## 19.2 Data Platform

Raw landing/archive -\> cleaned/conformed -\> business-ready
facts/dimensions/data products.

Tenant/row/column security and pseudonymization are applied before
analyst/AI access.

Data catalog tracks ownership, classification, lineage, freshness,
completeness and quality state.

Reverse activation into operations uses typed domain commands/events,
never direct warehouse writes to OLTP.

![Figure 5. Permissioned, evaluated AI architecture with guarded tool
execution.](media/image5.png "Figure 5. Permissioned, evaluated AI architecture with guarded tool execution."){width="6.75in"
height="0.7761450131233596in"}

*Figure 5. Permissioned, evaluated AI architecture with guarded tool
execution.*

## 19.3 AI Platform

### AI operations and provider data boundary

Every AI execution records use_case_id, prompt_template_version,
system-policy version, model/provider/version, retrieval
snapshot/evidence IDs, tool schema version, safety policy version,
latency, cost and outcome.

Model or prompt changes pass offline evaluation and canary/online
evaluation before promotion. Drift monitors task success, groundedness,
safety-block rate, tool error and cost; thresholds trigger rollback to
the last approved model/prompt bundle.

Red-team findings are versioned governance artifacts with severity,
remediation owner and regression tests. High-risk tool classes require
human approval regardless of model confidence.

Provider contracts must prohibit training on tenant content and require
the minimum feasible retention/no-retention mode. Restricted data may
only be sent to approved providers/regions with DPA/subprocessor
approval; tenant policy can disable specific providers/use cases.

Tenant data is never mixed in retrieval context, caches, fine-tunes or
evaluation datasets across tenants. Synthetic/de-identified evaluation
sets are preferred; production samples require explicit governance
approval and retention limits.

Use-case registry: owner, user role, purpose, allowed data classes, risk
tier, allowed tools, approval policy, budget, evaluation set and kill
switch.

Retrieval: authorize tenant/role/relationship/fields before search/read;
revalidate any cited record before response or tool use.

Model gateway: provider abstraction, model routing by
quality/latency/region/privacy/cost, fallback and circuit breaker.

Grounding: responses cite internal governed records/metrics and expose
freshness/uncertainty when relevant.

Tool execution: typed schema, dry-run/preview when feasible, domain
authorization, idempotency, approval for high-risk actions and immutable
audit.

Evaluation: offline golden sets plus online task success, acceptance,
groundedness, safety, latency, cost and business impact.

No model receives standing database credentials; no prompt can bypass
tenant authorization or tool policy.

Tenant-specific credentials live in a managed secret vault referenced by
IntegrationInstall; secret values never enter normal application
tables/logs.

Connector workers store sync cursor, provider version, last success,
retry state, reconciliation state and health metrics.

Uninstall/revoke must prove provider access/data flow stopped and
schedule cleanup according to retention policy.

Partner/provider-specific payloads are translated at the adapter
boundary; core domains never depend on provider field names.

## 20.2 Developer Platform

Public API is a product contract, not a direct mirror of internal
tables.

Sandbox tenants have simulated providers, deterministic test data and
safe webhook testing.

Developer apps use explicit scopes and tenant admin authorization; rate
limits and quotas are plan/partner aware.

SDKs are generated from versioned OpenAPI where practical; compatibility
tests run against supported SDK versions.

## 20.3 White-label and Mobile Fleet

White-label configuration is token/config/content driven. Semantic
safety colors, accessibility limits and Veyro AI semantic identity
cannot be overridden into ambiguity.

Published content/app configurations are immutable versions with
preview, approval, scheduling and rollback.

Branded app fleet tracks app/store owner, bundle/package ID,
certificates, privacy labels, release version, min supported version,
crash/adoption and store status.

Remote config/feature flags are signed/versioned and cannot grant a
capability not allowed by SaaS/tenant entitlement.

The KMP mobile fleet uses one shared feature and Compose Design System
codebase across Android/iOS; branded applications differ through
versioned configuration/assets/signing/capabilities, not copied feature
code.

androidApp and iosApp remain distinct store artifacts with independent
rollout, min-version and capability entitlement metadata; common code
version is traceable in every build artifact.

Platform-only SDKs are integrated behind ADR-017 adapters so
adding/replacing an Apple/Android provider does not contaminate common
feature modules.

# 21. Security, Privacy, Compliance & Threat Model

## 21.1 Security Architecture

### Mobile/local restricted-data controls

Shared SQLDelight stores holding Restricted/Confidential cache data use
SQLCipher or an equivalent encrypted SQLite driver. Database keys are
random per installation and wrapped by Android Keystore/iOS Keychain;
keys never enter common Compose state or backups.

iOS restricted caches use
NSFileProtectionCompleteUntilFirstUserAuthentication or stronger.
Android Auto Backup excludes restricted DBs/credentials. Logout, remote
session revocation and tenant removal purge keys and cached restricted
rows; stale encrypted files become unreadable.

Restricted mobile cache TTL defaults to 24 hours for coach/member
health/nutrition context unless an offline workflow justifies less.
Screenshot/recording protection is enabled for screens presenting
Restricted health/financial/biometric content where platform capability
permits.

Mobile API connections use a reviewed TLS public-key pinning policy with
at least one backup pin and a signed emergency-rollover mechanism. App
Attest/Play Integrity is required for rotating access-credential
issuance and other abuse-sensitive device endpoints, with graceful
manual fallback for unsupported legitimate devices.

### Key lifecycle

Root: environment-specific KMS CMKs with least-privilege key policies.
Tenant/data-class KEKs are envelope-encrypted under the root; Restricted
subject/media DEKs are generated per object/subject envelope as
appropriate.

Scheduled KEK rotation at least annually and immediate rotation on
compromise; DEKs are rewrapped without decrypting business plaintext at
application boundaries. Key version is stored with ciphertext and
decrypt policy is auditable.

Crypto-shredding destroys the wrapped DEK for data that cannot be
physically removed before backup/event expiry, after legal-hold checks.
A deletion certificate references key-destruction evidence and
residual-retention expiry.

Zero-trust service identity: workloads use short-lived IAM/service
credentials; no shared static database passwords in code or CI.

TLS in transit; managed encryption at rest; KMS key policies separated
by environment and high-risk data class where appropriate.

Secrets in managed vault with rotation and access audit. Customer
integration secrets are tenant-bound references.

WAF/rate limiting/bot controls at edge; application rate limits by
tenant/user/API key and operation risk.

Secure SDLC: peer review, SAST, dependency/container/IaC/secret
scanning, DAST for exposed surfaces, penetration testing and
vulnerability SLAs.

Production data access is just-in-time, purpose-bound and audited;
support has no standing unrestricted customer content access.

Mobile secure storage uses platform-protected Keystore/Keychain
adapters; tokens, device secrets and signing material are never stored
in shared SQLite, logs or Compose state restoration.

Common KMP code treats rooted/jailbroken/device-integrity signals as
risk inputs only; any blocking policy is server/configuration governed
and must preserve recovery/support paths.

Native payment, wallet, health, camera and biometric SDK callbacks cross
into shared code only through typed minimal-data adapters; raw provider
objects and secrets do not escape the platform boundary.

## 21.4 Privacy and Consent

ConsentRecord stores purpose, document/policy version, language,
subject/guardian, signed_at, evidence hash/reference, withdrawal and
source.

Purpose limitation is enforced in authorization/tool/search policies;
"has access" is insufficient without permitted purpose for restricted
data.

DSAR workflow handles access, correction, portability, restriction and
deletion with identity verification, legal hold and subprocessor
propagation.

Retention policies are data-class and region/version specific; jobs
produce deletion/retention evidence and do not silently ignore failures.

## 21.5 Jordan Privacy Baseline and Controller/Processor Model

Jordan launch baseline is Personal Data Protection Law No. (24) of 2023
and the regulations/instructions issued under it. The law has been in
force since 17 March 2024; compliance operations therefore ship in
Foundation rather than being deferred to Enterprise.

For gym member/staff data processed on tenant instructions, the gym is
normally controller and Veyro processor. Veyro is controller for its own
SaaS account, security, fraud, billing and service-improvement data only
to the extent documented in the privacy notice/DPA. Mixed roles are
recorded by processing purpose.

Each tenant receives a DPA/subprocessor disclosure, processing-purpose
inventory, retention schedule and DSAR workflow. DPIA/privacy review is
mandatory before health, biometric, AI profiling or new cross-border
sharing is enabled.

Primary Jordan hosting is AWS Bahrain (me-south-1), with UAE
(me-central-1) as DR. This is cross-border processing from Jordan and
cannot be enabled solely by architecture assumption; legal
basis/permit/contract requirements are a launch gate owned by privacy
counsel/DPO.

# 22. Reliability, Observability, SLOs, Capacity & FinOps

## 22.1 Observability Standard

OpenTelemetry traces across gateway, domain command, workflow, event
consumer and provider adapter with correlation_id/causation_id.

Metrics include technical RED/USE plus business signals such as payment
success, access denial reason, booking conflict, message delivery and
tenant impact.

Logs are structured and redacted; restricted data is prohibited. Tenant
ID may be a controlled attribute but user-provided labels are sanitized.

Every alert links to owner/runbook and includes affected tenants/regions
where safe.

Synthetic journeys continuously test sign-in, member lookup, booking,
payment sandbox, check-in decision and key provider paths.

## 22.2 Backpressure and Failure Isolation

Separate worker pools/queues for payments, notifications,
search/indexing, integrations, migrations, AI and low-priority
analytics.

Per-tenant concurrency/rate limits prevent one tenant from exhausting
shared resources.

Circuit breakers around provider adapters; degraded status shown in
product/control plane.

Bulk operations are chunked, resumable and report partial success rather
than holding giant transactions.

## 22.3 FinOps

Planning estimate (not a vendor quote): shared Foundation/V1 platform at
the envelope above targets approximately USD 1.5k-3.5k/month of core
cloud infrastructure before variable messaging/payment/AI charges,
assuming managed Postgres with cross-region replica, ECS/Fargate, Redis,
SQS/EventBridge, S3 and observability. Re-price quarterly with the cloud
calculator and real utilization.

Cost attribution tags every job/API/event/storage object/provider
dispatch with tenant/cost_category. Target infrastructure COGS is
tracked per active tenant/location/member and compared with plan
revenue; an architecture change that materially increases fixed baseline
cost requires a FinOps ADR review.

## 22.4 V1 Capacity and Partitioning Envelope

High-volume PostgreSQL tables use monthly range partitions where
write/query profiles justify it: access_event, audit_record,
ledger_posting, outbox_event and message/event-delivery history. Hot
operational retention is typically 90 days; older immutable evidence is
archived to S3 according to classification/legal policy and remains
queryable through controlled retrieval.

Indexes are tenant-leading for tenant-scoped access patterns. Partition
pruning, autovacuum, bloat, index size and archival lag are capacity
SLOs; a partition is created ahead of time and missing-future-partition
is a release/operations alert.

# 23. Deployment Topology, Environments & Infrastructure

![Figure 6. AWS reference production topology (logical architecture
remains
portable).](media/image6.png "Figure 6. AWS reference production topology (logical architecture remains portable)."){width="6.75in"
height="5.350561023622047in"}

*Figure 6. AWS reference production topology (logical architecture
remains portable).*

## 23.1 Environment and Account Model

Separate cloud accounts/projects for production, staging and
non-production/shared tooling; no prod data copied to lower environments
without approved anonymization.

Production uses at least two availability zones. Critical managed data
stores use multi-AZ replication and point-in-time recovery.

Secrets/KMS keys, event topics, databases, buckets and search indexes
are environment isolated.

Preview/test environments use synthetic tenants and provider sandboxes.

## 23.2 Network

Public edge: CDN/WAF/DDoS -\> load balancer/API gateway. Application and
data workloads remain in private subnets.

Database/cache/search accept traffic only from approved workload
security groups/identities.

Outbound provider calls use controlled egress/NAT and domain
allowlisting where practical; webhook callbacks enter through dedicated
validated endpoints.

Administrative production access uses SSO, short-lived credentials and
audited session mechanisms; no permanent bastion passwords.

## 23.3 Database and Backup

Managed PostgreSQL multi-AZ, PITR, encrypted snapshots, tested restore
automation and capacity alarms.

Connection pooling/proxy prevents serverless/web fanout from exhausting
database connections.

Read replicas may serve reporting/read-heavy projections but never relax
tenant policy or serve stale consequence-bearing authorization without
explicit freshness rules.

Backups are cross-region/copied according to continuity tier and legal
residency; restoration tests are scheduled and measured.

## 23.4 Jordan Primary and Warm-DR Topology

Primary: AWS me-south-1 (Bahrain), three-AZ capable region.
Product/control APIs, primary RDS PostgreSQL, Redis and queues run here.
DR: me-central-1 (UAE) with pre-created network/IAM/KMS/secrets/app
definitions and Tier-1 cross-region PostgreSQL replica.

S3 uses cross-region replication for required objects. Redis is treated
as rebuildable. SQS/EventBridge is not authoritative; the Postgres
outbox and S3 event archive republish unacknowledged business events
after failover. Search in V1 is rebuilt from Postgres because it uses
Postgres FTS, eliminating a separate OpenSearch DR dependency.

Replication lag is continuously measured. The ≤5 minute RPO claim is
valid only while replica lag/health remains within budget; breach pages
SRE and changes the published disaster-recovery readiness state.
Quarterly game days promote the DR replica and measure actual RPO/RTO.

KMS/secrets are region-ready using replicated/paired key strategy and
secret copies with separate IAM. Edge devices trust a signed endpoint
set containing both regions and fail over only after
control-plane/incident authorization to avoid split brain.

# 24. CI/CD, Schema Evolution, Release & Rollback

## 24.1 Pipeline Gates

### Architecture enforcement gates

RLS lint: every tenant table tenant_id NOT NULL + policy + ENABLE/FORCE
RLS; runtime role cannot own/bypass. Negative isolation tests run with
production-equivalent role.

Module dependency/SQL lint: application modules may reference only their
owned table prefix/schema and approved read-model/application
interfaces; cross-domain raw SQL/ORM imports fail CI. For the four
intentional bidirectional pairs, §6.3 is the normative directed graph:
only the listed synchronous edge may import/call the opposite
application interface; the reverse edge must remain event-driven.

Event contract lint: every event referenced by flow/code exists in
AsyncAPI/JSON Schema registry; compatibility and classification changes
require owner approval.

Permission lint: API commands/queries declare action/resource/scope;
unregistered permission names fail build.

Screen contract lint: every V1 Screen ID from design registry maps to a
BFF/read model or typed command manifest row before feature release.

Format/lint/type checks and unit tests.

Domain contract tests, tenant-isolation tests, authorization tests and
financial invariant tests.

SAST, dependency, secret, container and IaC scanning; SBOM/provenance
generation.

Build signed immutable artifacts/images.

Integration tests with PostgreSQL/event/workflow/provider sandboxes.

API/event schema compatibility checks and migration safety checks.

Deploy to staging; run E2E/critical synthetic/load
subset/accessibility/localization gates.

Canary/percentage rollout with feature flags; monitor SLO/business
guardrails.

Promote or rollback; publish release metadata, migration state and
change notice.

Domain contract uniqueness lint: CI compares normalized
authoritative-entity sets, command inventories, published-event sets,
runbook IDs, SLI/SLO signals and failure/degraded-behavior vocabulary
across all 57 §10 domains. Identical command inventories or reused
RB-\<DOMAIN\> IDs across different domains fail unless an explicit
shared-contract exception is approved. Each domain SLI/SLO may name only
signals owned by that domain or an explicitly documented dependency;
foreign-domain vocabulary such as booking-capacity signals in a billing
SLO fails the lint. Failure/degraded-behavior text is checked by the
same ownership rule. This prevents silent cross-domain template,
telemetry or generation mis-assignment.

## 24.2 Database Migration Policy

Expand -\> migrate/backfill -\> switch reads/writes -\> contract.
Destructive contract happens only after all deployed versions stop using
old shape.

Large backfills are online/resumable jobs with progress and throttling;
never a single deployment transaction.

Every migration records owner, expected lock/write impact,
rollback/forward-fix strategy and data validation query.

Schema and application deployment ordering is tested against at least
previous supported version for rolling deploy compatibility.

## 24.3 Mobile Release Policy

Backend APIs preserve compatibility for minimum supported app versions;
server can expose capability/version negotiation.

Remote config controls rollout but cannot repair an incompatible API
contract.

Minimum supported version, optional/forced update and kill-switch policy
are explicit; forced update is reserved for security/critical
incompatibility.

White-label fleet release metadata is tracked per branded app and store.

The repository pins a tested Kotlin/KMP/Compose/Gradle/Xcode/AGP
compatibility matrix. Toolchain upgrades are isolated pull requests with
Android+iOS build, UI, accessibility and performance qualification
before merge.

Shared KMP modules are versioned in source/build provenance; Android and
iOS release trains may advance independently as long as both consume an
API-compatible shared revision and pass platform gates.

CI builds Android on Linux runners where possible and iOS on macOS/Xcode
runners. Release candidates require real-device smoke tests for platform
capability adapters and the critical offline flows.

A common-code change that touches serialization, local schema, sync,
auth, routing or shared Design System triggers both Android and iOS
regression suites even if the initiating feature is platform-specific.

# 25. Onboarding, Migration, Offboarding & Data Portability

## 25.1 Provisioning and Go-live

Tenant provisioning workflow creates tenant/organization, placement,
encryption/config defaults, SaaS subscription entitlements, first admin
identity and audit evidence.

Implementation readiness is a state machine/checklist with blocking
validation for payments, tax, memberships, staff, schedule, access,
communications and migration.

Go-live is an approved transition; production provider credentials and
hardware activation are not assumed from sandbox success.

## 25.2 Migration Framework

### Migration source adapters and finance opening balance

Adapter inventory starts with CSV/Excel canonical import, verified
legacy gym-management exports/APIs (including Virtuagym where
contractually available), and tenant-specific SQL/API adapters behind
the same staging model. A named source adapter is added only after its
real export/API contract is verified; no adapter bypasses staging,
validation or reconciliation.

Canonical staging separates identity/person, memberships/contracts,
outstanding invoices/credits/wallet, historical payments,
attendance/access history, bookings, coaching/nutrition artifacts and
opening inventory. Unknown source fields are preserved in a raw
immutable import blob for evidence.

Financial cutover requires an accountant-approved opening trial balance:
receivable, cash/provider clearing, tax, wallet/service-credit
liabilities, unearned revenue and earned-to-date schedules. Historical
data that cannot be reconstructed is imported as explicitly labelled
opening-balance journals, never fabricated line-level history.

Dry run produces counts, hashes, duplicate/merge cases, financial
control totals, access/booking eligibility samples and unresolved
rejects. Go-live requires signed reconciliation; delta migration after
final source freeze is idempotent.

Source adapters normalize CSV/Excel/competitor/API data into a versioned
staging model.

Dry run produces row-level validation, mapping decisions, duplicates,
financial totals, membership/credit balances and reject/quarantine
reports.

Import is idempotent using source_system + source_id mappings.
Re-running does not create duplicates.

Financial migration uses opening balances/journal strategy approved by
finance; historical payments are not fabricated as new provider
transactions.

Cutover supports delta import, freeze window where necessary,
reconciliation/sign-off and rollback plan.

## 25.3 Offboarding

## 25.4 Privacy Lifecycle and Tenant Relocation

DSAR access/correction/export/restriction/deletion is a Foundation
SEC-01 capability even though full commercial tenant offboarding remains
later-phase. Privacy rights therefore do not depend on Enterprise
offboarding scope.

Tenant relocation uses the §7.5 workflow and is available for
noisy-neighbour remediation, regional policy and enterprise dedicated
placement. Offboarding/export uses the same canonical export manifests
and control-total verification.

States: cancel requested -\> obligations/export -\>
credentials/integrations revoked -\> read-only/archive -\> retention -\>
deletion.

Export package includes documented schemas, files and checksums; export
generation is auditable and time-limited.

Deletion orchestrates domain stores, indexes, caches, object storage and
subprocessors while respecting legal hold/backups/retention.

Veyro SaaS billing termination and gym business data retention are
coordinated but remain separate sources of truth.

## 26.1 JoFotara/E-invoice Failure Handling

### Current regulatory baseline

Jordan invoicing regulation requires an invoice serial number and
recognizes electronic invoices generated by the National E-Invoicing
System or an integrated system. Veyro therefore treats fiscal
serial/provider acknowledgement as a server-authoritative legal artifact
and never labels a local queue ticket as a tax invoice.

The ISTD publishes current joining, invoice-organization and technical
linking manuals for the National Electronic Invoicing System.
Integration certification tests are versioned against the exact
manual/API revision used at launch; provider changes are treated as a
regional-pack contract change.

## 26.2 Jordan Privacy and Data Protection

Personal Data Protection Law No. (24) of 2023 is the Foundation
baseline. Sensitive data classification explicitly includes financial,
health, genetic and biometric data; Veyro's Restricted class maps to
these categories and triggers stronger access, retention, DPIA and
provider review.

Tenant onboarding captures controller identity, DPO/privacy contact
where applicable, processing purposes, subprocessors, cross-border
region disclosure and consent/policy versions. Data-subject rights are
routed through SEC-01 regardless of commercial plan.

## 26.3 Jordan Payment Rails and Cash Operations

Cash is a first-class tender with register/shift opening, paid-in/out,
expected-vs-actual close, variance approval and immutable ledger
postings.

CliQ is modeled through an InstantTransferProvider capability rather
than direct assumptions about JoPACC participant access. The adapter may
create/reference a transfer instruction when a banking/payment partner
supports it and must reconcile bank/provider confirmations before Veyro
marks payment final.

eFAWATEERcom is an optional Jordan BillPresentmentPaymentProvider
capability for tenants/use cases where commercial/provider access is
available. Billing domain remains provider-neutral and reconciles
external payment references idempotently.

Card/acquirer integrations remain PaymentProvider adapters; Veyro never
stores PAN/CVV and prefers hosted/tokenized PCI scope reduction.

## 26.4 Jordan Communications and Employment Extensions

WhatsApp integration models provider policy dynamically: opt-in/consent,
conversation/service-window state, template category/approval, language
and current provider error codes are adapter metadata, not hard-coded
assumptions. A policy change must not require domain-code changes.

Jordan Social Security / payroll statutory deductions are an OPS-05
regional payroll extension. Payroll calculations are versioned policy
data reviewed by local payroll/legal specialists; V1 may export verified
attendance/commission inputs without claiming a statutory payroll engine
until certified.

Veyro invoice is finalized in its own domain according to approved local
policy; fiscal submission state is tracked separately.

Submission uses idempotent fiscal document reference. Timeouts lead to
"submission pending/unknown", not duplicate submission.

Provider response/QR/reference is stored with immutable invoice version
and included in issued receipt/invoice presentation when required.

Failed/pending submissions surface operational cases and retry.
Reconciliation compares Veyro fiscal documents against provider
acknowledgements.

Credit/refund flows use legally correct credit/cancellation document
semantics rather than editing a previously issued invoice.

## 27.2 Property/Invariant Tests

Tenant A can never observe or mutate Tenant B resources across API,
search, cache, job, event and AI paths.

Ledger entries always balance per currency; repeating same idempotent
command cannot change economic result.

Booking capacity never falls below zero and duplicate waitlist promotion
cannot consume multiple seats.

Access offline decision cannot outlive signed snapshot/credential
validity and cannot silently bypass a revoked credential after
reconciliation.

Membership historical terms are not mutated by later price/policy
changes.

Every consequence-bearing command emits either the expected event(s) or
a recorded failure; no committed state with missing outbox event.

## 27.3 Test Data and Production-like Qualification

Automated tests use deterministic synthetic tenant factories that
generate Jordan/Arabic/English names, memberships, ledger histories,
access credentials, nutrition constraints and large datasets without
copying production PII.

Any production-derived diagnostic dataset requires approved
de-identification, purpose, expiry and access logging; direct production
database snapshots are prohibited in developer/test environments.

Quarterly restore tests cover PostgreSQL promotion/PITR reconciliation,
S3 object restore, queue republish from outbox/archive, workflow restart
from domain checkpoints, mobile/edge snapshot expiry and tenant
relocation. Results record measured RPO/RTO and data/control totals.

KMP commonTest is mandatory for shared use cases, ViewModels/state
reducers, network contract mapping, local persistence/sync and
localization/bidi primitives.

Critical Coach/Member journeys run as platform E2E on both Android and
iOS; shared UI coverage does not replace TalkBack/VoiceOver, store SDK,
background execution, camera/NFC, biometrics or payment integration
tests on real platform runtimes.

Cross-platform parity tests compare domain-visible outcomes and
analytics/command contracts rather than screenshot identity;
platform-native adaptations are allowed when behavior and Design System
semantics remain equivalent.

## 28.2 Incident Lifecycle

Detect and declare severity; identify affected
tenants/regions/capabilities.

Contain: kill switch/feature flag/circuit breaker/degraded mode as
appropriate.

Preserve evidence and assign incident commander/domain owners.

Communicate known facts through status/customer channels; do not
speculate.

Recover technical service and reconcile business/data state (payments,
access, queues, documents).

Validate SLO/business outcomes and end incident only when reconciliation
is complete.

Publish postmortem with root cause, contributing controls, action owners
and recurrence prevention.

## 28.3 PITR / State-Recovery Reconciliation Runbook

1\. Incident commander declares recovery mode, freezes
consequence-bearing writes and disables provider dispatch workers.

2\. Quarantine outbox rows and record provider/fiscal/event high-water
marks for the suspected lost window.

3\. Prefer forward fix/compensating migration. PITR requires explicit
approval when state cannot be safely repaired in place.

4\. Restore/promote database into isolated validation endpoint; do not
immediately resume external side effects.

5\. Diff restored state against payment/acquirer settlements, JoFotara
acknowledgements, S3 event archive, audit evidence and edge/device
events for the lost window.

6\. Reconstruct missing authoritative rows by replaying retained
business events/provider evidence or append correction records. Never
retry a payment/fiscal command merely because its local row disappeared.

7\. Rebuild projections/caches, then release outbox only after
dispatch-guard reconciliation proves already-completed effects will not
repeat.

8\. Re-enable writes in stages, monitor reconciliation controls, produce
incident evidence and update recovery assumptions with measured results.

## 29.1 Extraction Triggers for Microservices

A domain requires materially different availability/latency/isolation
than the core application (for example Access or public Payments
ingress).

Independent scaling materially reduces cost or risk and cannot be solved
by separate worker/process pools.

A dedicated team owns the domain and network contract maturity justifies
service ownership.

Regulatory/data-residency constraints require separate placement.

Failure isolation needs a separate blast radius.

Extraction is not performed merely because a module is "important". The
default remains explicit in-process domain boundary.

# Appendix D. Architecture QA Checklist & Final Acceptance Criteria

## D.1 P0 Conditions - Architecture Cannot Be Approved

Any plausible cross-tenant read/write/search/cache/file/event/AI leakage
path.

Any path that can double-charge, lose/rewrite ledger history, mark
unpaid money as paid, or produce unreconcilable financial state.

Any access path that can grant physical access without
authoritative/bounded policy and auditable entitlement evaluation.

Any design that stores raw card credentials/secrets/biometric data
without an explicit secure boundary and purpose.

Any destructive privacy/offboarding path that can delete before
legal/export/retention obligations or cannot prove deletion/revocation.

Any AI tool path that can bypass authorization/approval or access
arbitrary database/secrets.

Any single failure that can permanently lose Tier-1 financial/access
state without recovery evidence.

## D.2 P1 Conditions - Required Fix Before Implementation Baseline

Direct cross-domain table writes or unowned shared business tables.

Externally retryable mutation without idempotency semantics.

Provider integration without webhook verification, retry and
reconciliation.

Cross-domain/timer process without durable workflow/recovery strategy.

Missing optimistic concurrency or conflict handling on
consequence-bearing mutable records.

Critical offline flow without snapshot TTL, duplicate/conflict and
reconnect reconciliation.

Search/analytics/AI path that treats projections as authoritative for a
consequence-bearing mutation.

Schema migration/deployment strategy that cannot roll forward/backward
safely during rolling deploy.

Missing SLO/telemetry/runbook for a critical path.

Regional Jordan requirement implemented as irreversible core-domain
vendor/country coupling.

commonMain depending on Android/iOS SDK types or platform provider
objects, or a platform capability implemented without the ADR-017
adapter/native-interop boundary.

Critical KMP/Compose mobile flow that is not qualified on both Android
and iOS for accessibility, RTL/localization, offline behavior, platform
lifecycle and required native SDK integration.

## D.3 Reviewer Questions

Can every one of the 57 domains identify its source of truth,
transaction boundary and event contract?

Are all 432 requirements represented without architecture hand-waving or
phase-based deletion?

Does the tenant isolation model cover APIs, background jobs, events,
files, cache, search, telemetry and AI?

Can membership sale/payment/refund/dunning be replayed/retried without
double economic effects?

Can access continue safely during cloud/network failure and reconcile
afterward?

Does every provider adapter have authentication, idempotency, retry,
health and reconciliation semantics?

Does the architecture scale operationally before microservices are
introduced?

Are data classification, purpose, retention, consent and audit enforced
as runtime architecture, not policy prose only?

Can AI explain evidence and execute only within tenant/user/tool policy
with appropriate approval?

Can mobile/web clients evolve while APIs/schema deploy independently?

Can a tenant migrate in/out with reconciled balances, source mappings
and verifiable export/deletion?

Are SLO, DR, capacity and FinOps targets technically measurable and
attached to owners/runbooks?

Can Jordan-specific tax/payment/WhatsApp/access integrations change
without changing core domains?

Are the open decisions correctly isolated behind interfaces so vendor
selection does not force a redesign?

Does the KMP mobile architecture keep commonMain free of Android/iOS SDK
dependencies and keep every platform-only capability behind an explicit
adapter?

Can Coach and Member share Compose UI/state/data while retaining
independent app identity, permissions, analytics, navigation and store
release control?

Are Arabic RTL, TalkBack/VoiceOver, offline sync, push, biometrics,
camera/barcode, NFC, wallet/payment and background execution verified on
both platform runtimes rather than assumed from shared code?

Can a problematic platform integration use a native Android or
SwiftUI/UIKit escape hatch without forking domain/data logic or breaking
API/analytics parity?

## D.4 Final Architecture Acceptance Gate

### Independent audit remediation gate

All P0 findings from the 23 Aug 2026 adversarial audit must be
independently re-tested and closed; "addressed in document" is not
evidence of closure by itself.

All P1 findings required for implementation baseline must have an owned
artifact/test/runbook or a named external validation gate with a
deadline before the affected feature can enter Pilot.

Traceability must contain DESIGNED/PARTIAL/DEFERRED statuses with
evidence pointers; a mechanically uniform 432/432 blanket COVERED result
is considered an audit failure.

The screen-contract manifest must be generated from the canonical V1
design registry before feature implementation; no hand-invented Screen
IDs are accepted.

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Required final state\
  P0 = 0. P1 = 0 or explicitly accepted with owner/date and no V1
  blocker. Tenant-isolation tests, financial invariants, access/offline
  reconciliation, event/outbox consistency, migration strategy, SLO
  observability, security/privacy controls and Jordan V1 adapter
  contracts must all be technically implementable from this
  specification.**
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------

# Appendix F. UX-to-API Contract Artifact

The approved Veyro V1 design/prototype owns the canonical Screen IDs.
The implementation repository MUST materialize
contracts/ui/screen-contracts.yaml directly from the canonical
design-registry export and validate it against OpenAPI, AsyncAPI and the
frontend route registry.

Mandatory fields: screen_id, surface, route, primary_read_model,
queries\[\], commands\[\], realtime_channels\[\], permissions\[\],
assurance, masking_variant, offline_mode, expected_error_codes\[\],
empty/loading/error states and owner_domain.

Release gate: count(Screen IDs in the canonical design registry marked
V1) == count(screen-contract manifest rows) == count(frontend
route-registry V1 rows). Any mismatch is P1 and blocks feature freeze.
This architecture document deliberately specifies the contract and gate
instead of inventing Screen IDs not present in the source design
artifact.

# Appendix H. Capacity, Cost and Extraction Triggers

The V1 event transport remains queue-based until sustained
business-event throughput exceeds 1,000 events/s, a consumer requires
long-horizon ordered replay that the S3 archive cannot meet
operationally, or queue fan-out/operability becomes more expensive than
a managed streaming service.

PostgreSQL FTS/pg_trgm remains the search implementation until measured
p95 or corpus/permission-filtering cost exceeds the §22 SLO at 3×
projected peak; search stays behind an interface so OpenSearch can be
introduced without changing product contracts.

A business domain is extracted from the modular monolith only when it
independently needs stronger SLO/scale/isolation, has stable API/event
contracts, and extraction removes more operational risk than it adds.
Access decision is the first likely extraction because edge-local SLO
differs from general product APIs.
